# Review continuation, graph bootstrap and source-import boundary

**Direction:** Accepted bounded implementation scope derived from the 2026-10-23 autonomous delivery request

**Implementation:** Graph bootstrap is merged; immutable continuation/history has independent bounded engineering and actual own-PR continuation/navigation acceptance. Full slice/round and native/human gates remain open.

**Parents:** [Review loop](README.md), [architecture](../architecture.md)

## User outcomes

Reopen the same review, retain its original question and answer, inspect a newer pinned head explicitly, and ask a new question without moving old evidence. Use a small graph to orient within the prepared source and inspect the precise evidence behind its relationships. Subsequently enter a repository/worktree path to discover and import the corresponding GitHub PR or GitLab MR, preserving every changed-file disposition.

The first graph is intentionally limited to source structure. Full before/after one-hop callers/callees arrive in slice 04. No edge may imply more than its actual evidence. A graph-review account and a source-corrected account remain distinct under the [review protocol](../../rules/graph-first-review.md).

## Immutable snapshot history

A review has one stable identity tied to provider host/project/change identity. It retains immutable snapshots keyed by snapshotId; each records actual comparison base/head and content-hashed source manifest. Adding a snapshot never overwrites source, questions, replies, graph evidence or notification history. Different provider/project/change identity rejects as a different review, even if the branch or number matches.

The server exposes currentSnapshotId plus snapshot summaries. The existing single-snapshot query shape remains a compatibility projection: `snapshot` is the selected immutable snapshot, defaulting to currentSnapshotId. An explicit snapshotId query selects retained history; absent IDs return a typed missing-source result. All questions retain their original anchor; the UI shows complete snapshot-labeled discussion by default, with an optional selected-snapshot filter. Question reads and reply validation resolve the question's snapshot, not the current selection. An authorized late answer on an old snapshot is valid if its original attachment/generation and evidence remain valid.

`AddSnapshot` accepts an immutable verified manifest, command identity and expectedCurrentSnapshotId. Source acquisition/hash verification happens outside the dispatcher transaction; commit validates repository/change identity, records snapshot and atomically advances currentSnapshotId with a receipt. An identical existing snapshot is idempotent and does not silently rewind current selection. A different concurrent expected-current value rejects with a typed conflict and no partial mutation. The authoritative store never trusts only an external export file. Adding a snapshot produces no agent wake event.

Selecting history in the browser is private view state, not shared graph focus or a new domain command. Preserve selection/draft until an explicit choice; never carry an unresolved question submission onto a different snapshot. Follow-up uses a new anchored question with an optional immutable parentQuestionId in the same review; cross-snapshot follow-up states both identities rather than moving the parent's anchor. Existing command retries, receipts, cursor and unknown notification identity survive restart and source addition.

Migrate a pre-history aggregate by retaining its one snapshot and all original IDs, credentials, receipts, cursor and attempts. Migration is additive/idempotent and runs under the existing owner; a failed migration leaves recoverable original data. Test on copies before any owner-approved update of the active pilot. Never delete or reset the pilot database to make migration pass.

## Bootstrap graph

Expose a read-only graph projection through the review application's public query boundary. Stable node IDs derive from snapshot/side/path and optional exact hunk/span, never viewport positions. Nodes show before-left/after-right and change labels in text as well as color; each opens the immutable source view and preserves discussion identity. React Flow is the accepted renderer. Keyboard-accessible source/relationship controls and a textual relationship list offer the same evidence path.

Bootstrap edges are `comparison`, `contains` or `document_reference`, with an explicit label, source anchors and evidence method. Comparison links pair verified old/new paths (including rename metadata when available); containment references manifest/hunk ownership; document references need an actual link span and resolved target in the pinned repository objects. Missing, external or unavailable targets stay unresolved. Manually curated relationships are labeled as such, checked against pinned source and never presented as parser-produced call facts. Unsupported material remains an inspectable disposition. No source edge means not analyzed unless the relevant analyzer explicitly established a leaf.

The bootstrap may use a bounded owner-prepared multi-file manifest, built from verified Git objects without provider discovery, fetch or target execution. Include the complete changed-path inventory for its selected PR; show unsupported, missing or deliberately unprepared content with reason. Preparation is not general import and does not claim semantic coverage. Render an honest useful document graph for documentation PRs and file/hunk structure for code PRs. A graph incapable of explaining the selected task produces a review finding.

Read-only projection changes require no graph mutation protocol. Slice 04 later introduces annotations with a graph revision independent of unrelated discussion revisions, atomic CAS and source validation. Keep provenance-kind fields extensible without treating future semantic analysis as already delivered.

## Import boundary v1

The source-acquisition subsystem owns a pure validated import result; review-domain commands own admission. Import code must not open the review database or write UI state. Public inputs are a canonical local worktree path and an explicit resolved provider candidate when discovery is ambiguous. Public results carry provider kind (`github`/`gitlab`), host, source/target project, PR/MR number/URL/state, comparison base/head, content-derived snapshot identity, source entries and complete changed-file/hunk dispositions with unsupported reasons. Paths are repository-relative; provider credentials, remote URL credentials and host session metadata never enter the manifest.

Resolve path/branch/remotes through Git read-only commands and existing authenticated `gh`/`glab` or existing connector capabilities. Never interpolate repository values into shell programs; pass argument arrays. Do not silently install tools or assume a host. For forks, match both source project/branch and target project. Return explicit zero, one or multiple matches; show candidates and require an explicit selection when ambiguous. Detached/default branches without a unique association remain unresolved. Authentication/tool availability gates only the affected provider route. Never guess the latest PR/MR.

Use the provider's actual comparison baseline semantics, not a guessed branch tip. Verify available commit objects and object type; fetch only missing verified refs into task-owned source storage when authorized and supported, without switching or changing the user's checkout. Read blobs without executing hooks, submodules or source code. Enforce bounded file/byte/hunk budgets; retain a truthful oversized/binary/submodule/missing disposition rather than silently dropping coverage. Strict UTF-8/blob rules from slice 01 remain applicable to selectable text.

The importer may produce a validated result while history/graph work proceeds. Only the integration owner maps it to `AddSnapshot`/initial preparation through durable ingress after contract tests agree. Import itself becomes a durable bounded job in slice 03: accepted request, process launch and result admission are separate. A job cannot hold a database transaction while acquiring source. Stable invocation identity and uncertain-launch reconciliation apply from first use.

## Preserved authentication boundary

Passkey usability is a known issue deferred to the final follow-up after slices 01–08. Preserve existing login, credentials, stored reviews and exact-session pairing now. No authentication redesign or iCloud-plugin modification is a prerequisite for graph, history, import, story or evidence work. Deferral does not authorize disabling existing access controls.

## Bootstrap derivation contract (02A)

Manual preparation accepts the legacy single `path`, or explicit unique `paths` to prepare multiple changed paths. Multi-file preparation reads the complete `git diff --name-status --no-renames` inventory between the pinned commits. Each entry retains status, old/new path, per-side disposition and reason; unselected, absent, binary, non-text and over-budget material stays visible. Added/deleted files have only their existing side; they must never receive invented empty source objects. Legacy single-path preparation continues to reject unavailable selected blobs rather than silently changing its snapshot identity.

The source manifest may additionally retain bounded inline Markdown references. Each reference includes the literal link destination, exact link-line anchor, resolution method and either a validated same-side target anchor or an unresolved reason. Only a conservative subset of inline Markdown links outside fenced/inline/indented code is analyzed; reference-style/HTML links, container text and executable semantics are not analyzed. Relative destinations resolve from the source document directory in the pinned object, with URI decoding and repository containment checks. External URLs, missing paths/fragments, unavailable text and limits remain unresolved. Reading a referenced target is one-hop evidence acquisition, not recursive graph traversal. Prepared referenced files outside the changed inventory are labeled context. If a link prepares another changed side, its disposition becomes prepared with referenced-blob provenance. Identity includes the inventory and references as well as source hashes.

The public application query derives a read-only source graph from that manifest: file nodes, contiguous changed-span nodes, comparison edges for verified pairs, containment edges and document-reference edges. Every node has exact source anchors or a visible unavailable disposition. Every edge carries evidence kind/method and source anchors. Stable IDs derive from snapshot/side/path/span. The graph carries `not analyzed` for callers/callees and unsupported Markdown forms, never a semantic leaf assertion. Comparison work is bounded; over-budget line analysis remains an explicit unknown while complete prepared source stays inspectable.

React renders a complete changed-file index and focused before-left/after-right pair, with one selected changed span at a time, to avoid shrinking the whole graph into unreadable text. The same graph has a keyboard-accessible node and relationship evidence list. Opening source updates explicit path/span selection, preserves question identity and offers return to graph. Missing sides show an absence disposition. Selection across files does not silently move a nonempty draft: the reviewer must clear/save it before choosing a new source. No graph action schedules a notification.


## Current structure reflection

**Observation:** The bounded implementation has a pure source/anchor domain, one transactional store, an authenticated gateway, a public React application bridge and a managed integration registry. Source acquisition remains an external immutable input. This is sufficient for the current product and keeps browser rendering from scheduling external work.

**Best rebuild design now:** Retain those responsibility boundaries and a single authoritative database owner. Derive the source graph from immutable source facts at the application query boundary, keep viewport/expansion private, and keep the graph renderer ignorant of delivery policy. An independent graph store would create duplicate identity and mutation machinery for a read-only projection; a semantic parser abstraction would falsely expand this bootstrap's analyzed scope. Neither is justified now. Before adding history, retain snapshots explicitly rather than overloading the displayed source selection as mutable review identity.

**Verified limits:** Current graph nodes use bounded source-heading/change excerpts rather than authored explanation. File relationships show structural evidence and do not establish why the change exists. A fresh reviewer must judge whether that orientation actually reduces assembly work; screenshots and click tests cannot establish it. The whole-product docs-only audit and independent engineering review remain separate acceptance gates.

## Review-driven bootstrap corrections

**Accepted correction:** A Markdown fence retains its opening marker and length; only a closing fence of the same marker with at least that length ends it. Inline code, indented code and fenced examples are outside analyzed document-reference text. Graph projection checks the same parsed provenance, so a plausible anchor inside code cannot become an edge.

A prepared side of a modified/type-changed file whose comparison side is unavailable is `not analyzed`, never all-added/all-removed. Those labels are valid only for an inventory-proven addition/deletion or an actual bounded comparison. Such a file has no inferred changed-span nodes. The source remains inspectable with an explicit comparison limitation.

Preparation retains its validated owner input atomically with the authoritative database preparation, allowing database-only recovery after either export fails. For earlier multi-file aggregates without that setup record, recover the original explicit selection from all explicitly selected side dispositions, including unsupported/missing sides. Exclude only deliberately unprepared sides and context-only prepared sides; referenced context must not become the selected input. Regenerate the same snapshot before restoring exports. Preserve discussion/receipts and reject conflicting inputs rather than resetting state.

The initial fit-all graph was observed unreadable on the forty-path implementation PR. Replace that layout with a complete scrollable changed-file index and a focused before/after file pair. Graph focus is private view state independent of source selection/drafts; choosing an index row does not retarget a question. Optional source-context expansion includes bounded directly related nodes, labels omitted visual neighbors, and retains the full evidence list. Scope is complete through the inventory; a focused view does not assert that other files are irrelevant. Source-open and return preserve focus and immutable source identity. This correction improves legibility without claiming semantic grouping or authored story narration.


Read-only Git preparation must disable automatic lazy fetch and replacement objects at both process environment and command level, use no system/global configuration, prompts, optional locks, hooks or filesystem monitors, and retain bounded time/output. A missing promisor object is unavailable evidence; it may never invoke a repository-configured fetch/upload-pack helper. Changed inventory is literal, rename-disabled and independent of relative/order/submodule-ignore settings; no external diff/text conversion runs. This repairs an actual reproduced helper-execution gap, not a permission to fetch missing source.

URL path and fragment syntax is separated before percent-decoding each component. An encoded `%23` identifies a literal `#` in a Git blob path; only a literal URL `#` introduces a fragment. Preparation and graph provenance validation use the same resolver and exact target/heading check.

## Readable bounded graph expansion

**Accepted correction:** A complete immutable graph projection does not require rendering every fact simultaneously. The file index accounts for the whole change; changed-span expansion exposes a complete labeled span selector but draws one chosen span with its before/after owner pair. Visible and total span counts remain explicit. Choosing a graph span never opens source, alters an anchor, retargets a draft or schedules delivery. Source access remains an explicit action. Context and span expansion are separate focused views so their combination cannot force all nodes back into miniature text.

The rationale is observed: a file with nineteen changed spans remained unreadable when fit-all was applied despite its readable default pair. Bound the visible projection and preserve all facts/anchors in selectors and the evidence list. Successor relation/context expansion must preserve this legibility invariant instead of reintroducing fit-all as coverage grows. This is a presentation choice, not deletion of evidence or semantic grouping.

Source presentation orders panes by side, always Before/base left and After/head right. A deleted file shows real base content on the left and an explicit absent/unprepared head on the right; an added file does the converse. Absence cannot swap spatial meaning or invent source content.


**Reference coverage limit:** The bootstrap has a global first-120-link analysis budget. It does not retain exact omitted paths or a count of links beyond that bound. The warning means remaining links are not analyzed; the unresolved list contains only attempted references, not an inventory of all omitted relationships. Complete changed-path inventory, explicit selected input, prepared one-hop context and analyzed link coverage are distinct sets. A literal resolved same-side document link proves a source reference only, not a semantic dependency. Successor analyzers must preserve these distinctions rather than treating a small unresolved count as complete coverage.

## Continuation derivation contract (02B)

**02A delivery:** PR21 merged at `cd8715ad2f848c444f952919ce019e7b1e913538` from reviewed `857fb072aaba095b9dadbfac4dcf11ff914eacdc`. Bounded engineering and presentation accepted; full slice/native/human acceptance remains open.

The authoritative review retains a current snapshot ID and immutable snapshots. Public review reads expose only the selected `snapshot` and lightweight `snapshotSummaries` (ID, title, base/head), plus currentSnapshotId; they do not duplicate every retained source body. A missing requested snapshot returns `source_unavailable`. Discussion remains complete with per-question immutable snapshot labels, so switching source never hides provenance. Explicit history selection is private state; the initially chosen snapshot stays selected when another becomes current. An explicit current/history choice is needed to move. Nonempty drafts, unresolved submission identity and in-flight submits hold snapshot selection. Follow-up starts a separate question with immutable optional parentQuestionId in the same review, preserving both source identities.

Overlapping read-only snapshot choices use latest-choice ownership. A superseded/aborted choice cannot restore its prior target after a newer choice succeeds. If the newest choice fails, restore the last displayed immutable snapshot rather than another unconfirmed request target. Subsequent polling must agree with the displayed selection; stale completions cannot silently retarget source or a draft.

An explicit selection owns its read until success, genuine failure or a newer explicit choice. Periodic observation pauses during that read and cannot abort/replace it merely because a polling interval elapsed. The bridge exposes selection loading separately from command submission; new composition/submission is held while source selection is unresolved. The newest owner alone releases that loading state. On completion, polling resumes against the committed displayed selection, with no false source-unavailable result for a successful slow read.

`AddSnapshot` is a local-user command: commandId, reviewId, expectedCurrentSnapshotId and verified snapshot. Active agents may read authorized historical source and reply to historical questions but cannot admit or replace snapshots. Admission validates source content hashes, line bounds, duplicate paths and manifest shape before the transaction; the atomic transition checks stable review identity and expected-current, appends the snapshot and advances current. An identical existing snapshot returns an applied receipt without rewinding current or creating a new revision/wake event; same ID with different content is `snapshot_conflict`. A stale expected-current for a new snapshot is `current_snapshot_conflict`. Different provider/host/target-project/change identity is `review_identity_conflict`. Reusing a command ID with another payload remains command_conflict.

Stable review identity is provider, host, target project and change number/URL. Source project/branches, provider state and actual baseline method are retained per snapshot and may not be silently narrowed. Legacy manual snapshots derive GitHub identity from their existing repository/PR URL. Additive manifest fields preserve source object IDs, rename/copy status, old/new paths/modes, per-side dispositions, hunks, coverage and acquisition counts. The acquisition subsystem owns provider/Git verification; domain admission owns content consistency and immutable review membership. Admission does not claim provider discovery occurred.

The encoded HTTP command envelope is bounded to 8 MiB, including JSON overhead and manifest metadata. This differs from acquisition's per-blob/total-content bounds. Oversized envelopes reject before dispatch; existing 16 KiB question and 64 KiB reply limits remain unchanged. Hash/schema/source validation occurs before the short database transaction. Rejected valid commands retain receipts; malformed/authentication envelopes do not gain domain access.

Migration adds history to the existing aggregate atomically and idempotently, preserving its revision, original snapshot, IDs, question/reply bodies, attachment, credentials, command receipts, inbox cursors, preparation input and attempt identities. Existing exports remain regenerable. Only a copy of an old database is used for migration tests. Startup verifies original prepared source against retained history and exports the authoritative current snapshot; it never makes the original preparation input rewind current. A failed migration rolls back its aggregate changes and retains recoverable original data.

Question queries resolve the question's snapshot. Reply evidence must belong to that snapshot; current selection has no role in reply validation. Attachment authorization/generation is still checked at apply time, and adding source does not replace that attachment. Follow-up parent IDs must resolve within the same review; invalid/missing parents reject without retargeting the original question. History admission creates no inbox item or notification attempt.

The [persisted-format and legacy identity contract](persistence-compatibility.md) defines physical legacy/current records, migration discrimination, exact source/hash/reason conventions and retry vectors required for a compatible rebuild.

## Verified preparation and identity schemes

Manual preparation and admission share the `source-preparation` public boundary. Scripts orchestrate owner/runtime work; this boundary reads bounded pinned Git objects and produces/validates the manifest without opening SQLite. The gateway verifies a declared `manual_git_v1` manifest outside transactions by reconstructing the original explicit selection, rebuilding actual source/ledger/references from the pinned objects, and comparing canonical values. It does not trust an owner JSON claim that acquisition was verified.

`manual_git_v1` preserves the delivered identity algorithm: SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON using the construction order below. Its legacy field order is part of compatibility, not the incoming JSON object's property order. Permuting input object properties must not change verification. Existing stored IDs remain opaque and unchanged; neither schema parsing nor migration invents a replacement ID. New IDs/content/provenance that fail the known scheme reject.

| Identity value | Compatibility order and meaning |
|---|---|
| Root | baseSha, headSha, sources; multi-file additionally changedFiles, documentReferences. Review aliases/title are outside this hash but remain part of the canonical verified manifest. |
| Source | path, side, content, lineCount, hash. Single-path order is base then head. Multi-file follows literal changed-inventory order, base then head where present; referenced context appends in encountered link order. Hash is SHA-256 of original decoded UTF-8 content. |
| Changed file | status, oldPath, newPath, dispositions; each disposition is side, path, state, reason. Multi-file manual preparation does not infer renames or synthesize imported modes/hunks. |
| Reference | destination, source anchor, target anchor or null, method, reason. Anchors order snapshotId, side, path, startLine, endLine. During identity construction snapshotId is the literal placeholder `pending`; actual IDs replace it only after hashing. |

The preparation boundary reconstructs the original manual input from the manifest for verification and legacy database-only recovery. Explicit selection includes unsupported/missing side dispositions and prepared sides marked as directly verified; deliberately unprepared and context-only referenced sides are excluded. This rule has one owner so recovery and admission cannot silently disagree about selected paths.

A successful verifier issues an internal nonserialized witness bound to the review ID and exact canonical manifest. The store accepts new source only with that matching witness, then performs CAS/authorization atomically. A serialized flag, forged object, witness from another review, or witness paired with changed content cannot authorize admission. Failed verification still produces a durable rejected receipt for a valid authenticated command. Idempotent exact retained-snapshot/receipt reads need no new Git acquisition and never rewind current.

The importer-v1 algorithm remains distinct: provider host/target/source projects/change, actual baseline/head, ordered source object/hash entries and complete ledger/hunks determine its existing ID. The slice03 candidate adapter verifies that exact scheme and provenance through this same public boundary, separately from manual admission. Raw provider JSON cannot obtain its witness; acquisition is invoked through its public port. Source object IDs/modes/hunks/counts remain losslessly representable for that successor.

## Continuation structure reflection

**Observed structure:** The database owns one review aggregate and separate receipt/credential/setup tables. Retained snapshots and currentSnapshotId are durable; selected snapshot, graph focus and draft are private presentation state. Historical queries return one source body plus complete discussion and lightweight history, while an active attachment remains authorized by its current generation rather than by which head is displayed. Git verification is an effect outside the transaction and cannot be replaced by a caller's JSON assertion.

**Best rebuild design now:** Keep the atomic aggregate for this bounded local review and extract preparation as its own effect boundary with pure domain admission policy. This preserves one consistency boundary for source addition, discussion and receipts, and makes actual pinned-source verification independently testable. A normalized snapshot table could reduce write/read amplification for large histories, but requires a deliberate schema migration and equivalent atomic query semantics; repeated immutable source in the current aggregate is a known scaling cost, not a reason to add a second writer now. Public selected-source queries already avoid sending all history bodies to React/MCP. No unlimited-history performance claim is made.

The witness separates verified acquisition from raw transport without serializing a forgeable authority flag. Versioned identity adapters preserve compatibility better than recomputing IDs from parsed object order or forcing all providers into the legacy manual hash. Future acquisition and analysis must enter through verified public ports, preserve exact provenance and use independent job identity; they cannot turn setup input persistence into an import job or silently retarget historical anchors. These are accepted current boundaries, not evidence that the successor routes already run.


## Observed continuation presentation limits

The accepted bounded journey distinguishes durable current, private selected snapshot and immutable question source: an original-head question remains answerable after another head is admitted, while a separate follow-up can explicitly anchor the newer head without moving its parent. Complete discussion exposes both source identities and the parent relation. The snapshot URL restores the selected immutable snapshot on reload; it does not persist every file/span/viewport choice. Precise evidence is reopened through the saved question/reply link. Draft holding and graph focus remain separate from those durable relations.

Independent graph-first investigation found the file inventory and structural source navigation useful and honest, but establishing admission → verification → persistence → selection → discussion policy still required multiple source views. Literal document edges do not prepare that semantic account. Repetitive import/type previews and first-hunk defaults provide limited prioritization, and raw snapshot/parent IDs impose comparison work. These are retained presentation limits; bounded history acceptance does not establish full prepared semantic understanding or unfamiliar-human comprehension. Source assertions, external test receipts, controlled participant replies and native turn evidence remain distinct.

The exact persisted primary comparison keys and manual/provider structural file/hunk IDs, including null-side and copied-source cases, are specified by [structural identity compatibility](persistence-compatibility.md#structural-comparison-identity-compatibility). General snapshot/side/path/span descriptions do not replace those encodings.

Existing command retries, receipts, cursor and unknown notification identity survive restart and source addition.

Migrate a pre-history aggregate by retaining its one snapshot and all original IDs, credentials, receipts, cursor and attempts. Migration is additive/idempotent and runs under the existing owner; a failed migration leaves recoverable original data. Test on copies before any owner-approved update of the active pilot. Never delete or reset the pilot database to make migration pass.

## Bootstrap graph

Expose a read-only graph projection through the review application's public query boundary. Stable node IDs derive from snapshot/side/path and optional exact hunk/span, never viewport positions. Nodes show before-left/after-right and change labels in text as well as color; each opens the immutable source view and preserves discussion identity. React Flow is the accepted renderer. Keyboard-accessible source/relationship controls and a textual relationship list offer the same evidence path.

Bootstrap edges are `comparison`, `contains` or `document_reference`, with an explicit label, source anchors and evidence method. Comparison links pair verified old/new paths (including rename metadata when available); containment references manifest/hunk ownership; document references need an actual link span and resolved target in the pinned repository objects. Missing, external or unavailable targets stay unresolved. Manually curated relationships are labeled as such, checked against pinned source and never presented as parser-produced call facts. Unsupported material remains an inspectable disposition. No source edge means not analyzed unless the relevant analyzer explicitly established a leaf.

The bootstrap may use a bounded owner-prepared multi-file manifest, built from verified Git objects without provider discovery, fetch or target execution. Include the complete changed-path inventory for its selected PR; show unsupported, missing or deliberately unprepared content with reason. Preparation is not general import and does not claim semantic coverage. Render an honest useful document graph for documentation PRs and file/hunk structure for code PRs. A graph incapable of explaining the selected task produces a review finding.

Read-only projection changes require no graph mutation protocol. Slice 04 later introduces annotations with a graph revision independent of unrelated discussion revisions, atomic CAS and source validation. Keep provenance-kind fields extensible without treating future semantic analysis as already delivered.

## Import boundary v1

The source-acquisition subsystem owns a pure validated import result; review-domain commands own admission. Import code must not open the review database or write UI state. Public inputs are a canonical local worktree path and an explicit resolved provider candidate when discovery is ambiguous. Public results carry provider kind (`github`/`gitlab`), host, source/target project, PR/MR number/URL/state, comparison base/head, content-derived snapshot identity, source entries and complete changed-file/hunk dispositions with unsupported reasons. Paths are repository-relative; provider credentials, remote URL credentials and host session metadata never enter the manifest.

Resolve path/branch/remotes through Git read-only commands and existing authenticated `gh`/`glab` or existing connector capabilities. Never interpolate repository values into shell programs; pass argument arrays. Do not silently install tools or assume a host. For forks, match both source project/branch and target project. Return explicit zero, one or multiple matches; show candidates and require an explicit selection when ambiguous. Detached/default branches without a unique association remain unresolved. Authentication/tool availability gates only the affected provider route. Never guess the latest PR/MR.

Use the provider's actual comparison baseline semantics, not a guessed branch tip. Verify available commit objects and object type; fetch only missing verified refs into task-owned source storage when authorized and supported, without switching or changing the user's checkout. Read blobs without executing hooks, submodules or source code. Enforce bounded file/byte/hunk budgets; retain a truthful oversized/binary/submodule/missing disposition rather than silently dropping coverage. Strict UTF-8/blob rules from slice 01 remain applicable to selectable text.

The importer may produce a validated result while history/graph work proceeds. Only the integration owner maps it to `AddSnapshot`/initial preparation through durable ingress after contract tests agree. Import itself becomes a durable bounded job in slice 03: accepted request, process launch and result admission are separate. A job cannot hold a database transaction while acquiring source. Stable invocation identity and uncertain-launch reconciliation apply from first use.

## Single local-owner access

The 2026-10-24 user correction supersedes the former deferred passkey/login requirement. The existing local/Tailscale workspace opens without manual credentials. The gateway derives the local owner while explicit participant credentials keep exact-session and attachment-generation routing checks. See [runtime access policy](runtime.md). Stored history and credentials, loopback/Host policy and the existing private Serve route are preserved. No alternate login or multi-user identity design is introduced.

## Bootstrap derivation contract (02A)

Manual preparation accepts the legacy single `path`, or explicit unique `paths` to prepare multiple changed paths. Multi-file preparation reads the complete `git diff --name-status --no-renames` inventory between the pinned commits. Each entry retains status, old/new path, per-side disposition and reason; unselected, absent, binary, non-text and over-budget material stays visible. Added/deleted files have only their existing side; they must never receive invented empty source objects. Legacy single-path preparation continues to reject unavailable selected blobs rather than silently changing its snapshot identity.

The source manifest may additionally retain bounded inline Markdown references. Each reference includes the literal link destination, exact link-line anchor, resolution method and either a validated same-side target anchor or an unresolved reason. Only a conservative subset of inline Markdown links outside fenced/inline/indented code is analyzed; reference-style/HTML links, container text and executable semantics are not analyzed. Relative destinations resolve from the source document directory in the pinned object, with URI decoding and repository containment checks. External URLs, missing paths/fragments, unavailable text and limits remain unresolved. Reading a referenced target is one-hop evidence acquisition, not recursive graph traversal. Prepared referenced files outside the changed inventory are labeled context. If a link prepares another changed side, its disposition becomes prepared with referenced-blob provenance. Identity includes the inventory and references as well as source hashes.

The public application query derives a read-only source graph from that manifest: file nodes, contiguous changed-span nodes, comparison edges for verified pairs, containment edges and document-reference edges. Every node has exact source anchors or a visible unavailable disposition. Every edge carries evidence kind/method and source anchors. Stable IDs derive from snapshot/side/path/span. The graph carries `not analyzed` for callers/callees and unsupported Markdown forms, never a semantic leaf assertion. Comparison work is bounded; over-budget line analysis remains an explicit unknown while complete prepared source stays inspectable.

React renders a complete changed-file index and focused before-left/after-right pair, with one selected changed span at a time, to avoid shrinking the whole graph into unreadable text. The same graph has a keyboard-accessible node and relationship evidence list. Opening source updates explicit path/span selection, preserves question identity and offers return to graph. Missing sides show an absence disposition. Selection across files does not silently move a nonempty draft: the reviewer must clear/save it before choosing a new source. No graph action schedules a notification.


## Current structure reflection

**Observation:** The bounded implementation has a pure source/anchor domain, one transactional store, an authenticated gateway, a public React application bridge and a managed integration registry. Source acquisition remains an external immutable input. This is sufficient for the current product and keeps browser rendering from scheduling external work.

**Best rebuild design now:** Retain those responsibility boundaries and a single authoritative database owner. Derive the source graph from immutable source facts at the application query boundary, keep viewport/expansion private, and keep the graph renderer ignorant of delivery policy. An independent graph store would create duplicate identity and mutation machinery for a read-only projection; a semantic parser abstraction would falsely expand this bootstrap's analyzed scope. Neither is justified now. Before adding history, retain snapshots explicitly rather than overloading the displayed source selection as mutable review identity.

**Verified limits:** Current graph nodes use bounded source-heading/change excerpts rather than authored explanation. File relationships show structural evidence and do not establish why the change exists. A fresh reviewer must judge whether that orientation actually reduces assembly work; screenshots and click tests cannot establish it. The whole-product docs-only audit and independent engineering review remain separate acceptance gates.

## Review-driven bootstrap corrections

**Accepted correction:** A Markdown fence retains its opening marker and length; only a closing fence of the same marker with at least that length ends it. Inline code, indented code and fenced examples are outside analyzed document-reference text. Graph projection checks the same parsed provenance, so a plausible anchor inside code cannot become an edge.

A prepared side of a modified/type-changed file whose comparison side is unavailable is `not analyzed`, never all-added/all-removed. Those labels are valid only for an inventory-proven addition/deletion or an actual bounded comparison. Such a file has no inferred changed-span nodes. The source remains inspectable with an explicit comparison limitation.

Preparation retains its validated owner input atomically with the authoritative database preparation, allowing database-only recovery after either export fails. For earlier multi-file aggregates without that setup record, recover the original explicit selection from all explicitly selected side dispositions, including unsupported/missing sides. Exclude only deliberately unprepared sides and context-only prepared sides; referenced context must not become the selected input. Regenerate the same snapshot before restoring exports. Preserve discussion/receipts and reject conflicting inputs rather than resetting state.

The initial fit-all graph was observed unreadable on the forty-path implementation PR. Replace that layout with a complete scrollable changed-file index and a focused before/after file pair. Graph focus is private view state independent of source selection/drafts; choosing an index row does not retarget a question. Optional source-context expansion includes bounded directly related nodes, labels omitted visual neighbors, and retains the full evidence list. Scope is complete through the inventory; a focused view does not assert that other files are irrelevant. Source-open and return preserve focus and immutable source identity. This correction improves legibility without claiming semantic grouping or authored story narration.


Read-only Git preparation must disable automatic lazy fetch and replacement objects at both process environment and command level, use no system/global configuration, prompts, optional locks, hooks or filesystem monitors, and retain bounded time/output. A missing promisor object is unavailable evidence; it may never invoke a repository-configured fetch/upload-pack helper. Changed inventory is literal, rename-disabled and independent of relative/order/submodule-ignore settings; no external diff/text conversion runs. This repairs an actual reproduced helper-execution gap, not a permission to fetch missing source.

URL path and fragment syntax is separated before percent-decoding each component. An encoded `%23` identifies a literal `#` in a Git blob path; only a literal URL `#` introduces a fragment. Preparation and graph provenance validation use the same resolver and exact target/heading check.

## Readable bounded graph expansion

**Accepted correction:** A complete immutable graph projection does not require rendering every fact simultaneously. The file index accounts for the whole change; changed-span expansion exposes a complete labeled span selector but draws one chosen span with its before/after owner pair. Visible and total span counts remain explicit. Choosing a graph span never opens source, alters an anchor, retargets a draft or schedules delivery. Source access remains an explicit action. Context and span expansion are separate focused views so their combination cannot force all nodes back into miniature text.

The rationale is observed: a file with nineteen changed spans remained unreadable when fit-all was applied despite its readable default pair. Bound the visible projection and preserve all facts/anchors in selectors and the evidence list. Successor relation/context expansion must preserve this legibility invariant instead of reintroducing fit-all as coverage grows. This is a presentation choice, not deletion of evidence or semantic grouping.

Source presentation orders panes by side, always Before/base left and After/head right. A deleted file shows real base content on the left and an explicit absent/unprepared head on the right; an added file does the converse. Absence cannot swap spatial meaning or invent source content.


**Reference coverage limit:** The bootstrap has a global first-120-link analysis budget. It does not retain exact omitted paths or a count of links beyond that bound. The warning means remaining links are not analyzed; the unresolved list contains only attempted references, not an inventory of all omitted relationships. Complete changed-path inventory, explicit selected input, prepared one-hop context and analyzed link coverage are distinct sets. A literal resolved same-side document link proves a source reference only, not a semantic dependency. Successor analyzers must preserve these distinctions rather than treating a small unresolved count as complete coverage.

## Continuation derivation contract (02B)

**02A delivery:** PR21 merged at `cd8715ad2f848c444f952919ce019e7b1e913538` from reviewed `857fb072aaba095b9dadbfac4dcf11ff914eacdc`. Bounded engineering and presentation accepted; full slice/native/human acceptance remains open.

The authoritative review retains a current snapshot ID and immutable snapshots. Public review reads expose only the selected `snapshot` and lightweight `snapshotSummaries` (ID, title, base/head), plus currentSnapshotId; they do not duplicate every retained source body. A missing requested snapshot returns `source_unavailable`. Discussion remains complete with per-question immutable snapshot labels, so switching source never hides provenance. Explicit history selection is private state; the initially chosen snapshot stays selected when another becomes current. An explicit current/history choice is needed to move. Nonempty drafts, unresolved submission identity and in-flight submits hold snapshot selection. Follow-up starts a separate question with immutable optional parentQuestionId in the same review, preserving both source identities.

Overlapping read-only snapshot choices use latest-choice ownership. A superseded/aborted choice cannot restore its prior target after a newer choice succeeds. If the newest choice fails, restore the last displayed immutable snapshot rather than another unconfirmed request target. Subsequent polling must agree with the displayed selection; stale completions cannot silently retarget source or a draft.

An explicit selection owns its read until success, genuine failure or a newer explicit choice. Periodic observation pauses during that read and cannot abort/replace it merely because a polling interval elapsed. The bridge exposes selection loading separately from command submission; new composition/submission is held while source selection is unresolved. The newest owner alone releases that loading state. On completion, polling resumes against the committed displayed selection, with no false source-unavailable result for a successful slow read.

`AddSnapshot` is a local-user command: commandId, reviewId, expectedCurrentSnapshotId and verified snapshot. Active agents may read authorized historical source and reply to historical questions but cannot admit or replace snapshots. Admission validates source content hashes, line bounds, duplicate paths and manifest shape before the transaction; the atomic transition checks stable review identity and expected-current, appends the snapshot and advances current. An identical existing snapshot returns an applied receipt without rewinding current or creating a new revision/wake event; same ID with different content is `snapshot_conflict`. A stale expected-current for a new snapshot is `current_snapshot_conflict`. Different provider/host/target-project/change identity is `review_identity_conflict`. Reusing a command ID with another payload remains command_conflict.

Stable review identity is provider, host, target project and change number/URL. Source project/branches, provider state and actual baseline method are retained per snapshot and may not be silently narrowed. Legacy manual snapshots derive GitHub identity from their existing repository/PR URL. Additive manifest fields preserve source object IDs, rename/copy status, old/new paths/modes, per-side dispositions, hunks, coverage and acquisition counts. The acquisition subsystem owns provider/Git verification; domain admission owns content consistency and immutable review membership. Admission does not claim provider discovery occurred.

The encoded HTTP command envelope is bounded to 8 MiB, including JSON overhead and manifest metadata. This differs from acquisition's per-blob/total-content bounds. Oversized envelopes reject before dispatch; existing 16 KiB question and 64 KiB reply limits remain unchanged. Hash/schema/source validation occurs before the short database transaction. Rejected valid commands retain receipts; malformed/authentication envelopes do not gain domain access.

Migration adds history to the existing aggregate atomically and idempotently, preserving its revision, original snapshot, IDs, question/reply bodies, attachment, credentials, command receipts, inbox cursors, preparation input and attempt identities. Existing exports remain regenerable. Only a copy of an old database is used for migration tests. Startup verifies original prepared source against retained history and exports the authoritative current snapshot; it never makes the original preparation input rewind current. A failed migration rolls back its aggregate changes and retains recoverable original data.

Question queries resolve the question's snapshot. Reply evidence must belong to that snapshot; current selection has no role in reply validation. Attachment authorization/generation is still checked at apply time, and adding source does not replace that attachment. Follow-up parent IDs must resolve within the same review; invalid/missing parents reject without retargeting the original question. History admission creates no inbox item or notification attempt.

The [persisted-format and legacy identity contract](persistence-compatibility.md) defines physical legacy/current records, migration discrimination, exact source/hash/reason conventions and retry vectors required for a compatible rebuild.

## Verified preparation and identity schemes

Manual preparation and admission share the `source-preparation` public boundary. Scripts orchestrate owner/runtime work; this boundary reads bounded pinned Git objects and produces/validates the manifest without opening SQLite. The gateway verifies a declared `manual_git_v1` manifest outside transactions by reconstructing the original explicit selection, rebuilding actual source/ledger/references from the pinned objects, and comparing canonical values. It does not trust an owner JSON claim that acquisition was verified.

`manual_git_v1` preserves the delivered identity algorithm: SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON using the construction order below. Its legacy field order is part of compatibility, not the incoming JSON object's property order. Permuting input object properties must not change verification. Existing stored IDs remain opaque and unchanged; neither schema parsing nor migration invents a replacement ID. New IDs/content/provenance that fail the known scheme reject.

| Identity value | Compatibility order and meaning |
|---|---|
| Root | baseSha, headSha, sources; multi-file additionally changedFiles, documentReferences. Review aliases/title are outside this hash but remain part of the canonical verified manifest. |
| Source | path, side, content, lineCount, hash. Single-path order is base then head. Multi-file follows literal changed-inventory order, base then head where present; referenced context appends in encountered link order. Hash is SHA-256 of original decoded UTF-8 content. |
| Changed file | status, oldPath, newPath, dispositions; each disposition is side, path, state, reason. Multi-file manual preparation does not infer renames or synthesize imported modes/hunks. |
| Reference | destination, source anchor, target anchor or null, method, reason. Anchors order snapshotId, side, path, startLine, endLine. During identity construction snapshotId is the literal placeholder `pending`; actual IDs replace it only after hashing. |

The preparation boundary reconstructs the original manual input from the manifest for verification and legacy database-only recovery. Explicit selection includes unsupported/missing side dispositions and prepared sides marked as directly verified; deliberately unprepared and context-only referenced sides are excluded. This rule has one owner so recovery and admission cannot silently disagree about selected paths.

A successful verifier issues an internal nonserialized witness bound to the review ID and exact canonical manifest. The store accepts new source only with that matching witness, then performs CAS/authorization atomically. A serialized flag, forged object, witness from another review, or witness paired with changed content cannot authorize admission. Failed verification still produces a durable rejected receipt for a valid authenticated command. Idempotent exact retained-snapshot/receipt reads need no new Git acquisition and never rewind current.

The importer-v1 algorithm remains distinct: provider host/target/source projects/change, actual baseline/head, ordered source object/hash entries and complete ledger/hunks determine its existing ID. The slice03 candidate adapter verifies that exact scheme and provenance through this same public boundary, separately from manual admission. Raw provider JSON cannot obtain its witness; acquisition is invoked through its public port. Source object IDs/modes/hunks/counts remain losslessly representable for that successor.

## Continuation structure reflection

**Observed structure:** The database owns one review aggregate and separate receipt/credential/setup tables. Retained snapshots and currentSnapshotId are durable; selected snapshot, graph focus and draft are private presentation state. Historical queries return one source body plus complete discussion and lightweight history, while an active attachment remains authorized by its current generation rather than by which head is displayed. Git verification is an effect outside the transaction and cannot be replaced by a caller's JSON assertion.

**Best rebuild design now:** Keep the atomic aggregate for this bounded local review and extract preparation as its own effect boundary with pure domain admission policy. This preserves one consistency boundary for source addition, discussion and receipts, and makes actual pinned-source verification independently testable. A normalized snapshot table could reduce write/read amplification for large histories, but requires a deliberate schema migration and equivalent atomic query semantics; repeated immutable source in the current aggregate is a known scaling cost, not a reason to add a second writer now. Public selected-source queries already avoid sending all history bodies to React/MCP. No unlimited-history performance claim is made.

The witness separates verified acquisition from raw transport without serializing a forgeable authority flag. Versioned identity adapters preserve compatibility better than recomputing IDs from parsed object order or forcing all providers into the legacy manual hash. Future acquisition and analysis must enter through verified public ports, preserve exact provenance and use independent job identity; they cannot turn setup input persistence into an import job or silently retarget historical anchors. These are accepted current boundaries, not evidence that the successor routes already run.


## Observed continuation presentation limits

The accepted bounded journey distinguishes durable current, private selected snapshot and immutable question source: an original-head question remains answerable after another head is admitted, while a separate follow-up can explicitly anchor the newer head without moving its parent. Complete discussion exposes both source identities and the parent relation. The snapshot URL restores the selected immutable snapshot on reload; it does not persist every file/span/viewport choice. Precise evidence is reopened through the saved question/reply link. Draft holding and graph focus remain separate from those durable relations.

Independent graph-first investigation found the file inventory and structural source navigation useful and honest, but establishing admission → verification → persistence → selection → discussion policy still required multiple source views. Literal document edges do not prepare that semantic account. Repetitive import/type previews and first-hunk defaults provide limited prioritization, and raw snapshot/parent IDs impose comparison work. These are retained presentation limits; bounded history acceptance does not establish full prepared semantic understanding or unfamiliar-human comprehension. Source assertions, external test receipts, controlled participant replies and native turn evidence remain distinct.

The exact persisted primary comparison keys and manual/provider structural file/hunk IDs, including null-side and copied-source cases, are specified by [structural identity compatibility](persistence-compatibility.md#structural-comparison-identity-compatibility). General snapshot/side/path/span descriptions do not replace those encodings.
