# Durable repository-path import jobs

**Contract revision:** `import-job-v1` (bounded launch/quota clarification; existing persisted/source identities unchanged)

**Direction:** Accepted bounded slice 03 design

**Implementation:** The bounded implementation has independent cumulative engineering, actual GitHub own-PR import/continuation/navigation and docs-only knowledge-readiness evidence. Its structural graph remains a source navigator, not a complete semantic explanation. Operational publication/deployment and full-round/native/human gates have separate receipts; do not infer them from implementation status.

**Parents:** [Review/source history](evolution.md), [existing contracts](contracts.md), [reactive ownership](../reactive-design.md)

## User journey

Enter a local repository/worktree path. The app discovers the corresponding PR/MR using existing authenticated provider tooling, presents an explicit choice when needed, shows progress, and opens a complete changed-file/hunk ledger after verified admission. A unique verified candidate can continue automatically because the request is to import that path; incomplete discovery never implies uniqueness. Multiple candidates, unavailable routes, detached/default branches and no match remain explicit. A reviewer can continue discussing an already open review while acquisition runs.

The product flow is path → choice/progress → review. Show concise human states and actionable errors; process journal rows and internal identities belong in diagnostics/evidence, not the primary flow. Imported source is immutable. A new head adds history only after the source and expected-current check pass; it never moves old questions, changes credentials or selects another agent session. The GitHub route uses existing `gh`; absent `glab` is an unavailable GitLab route, not permission to install it or infer GitLab success.

## Simple single-owner design

Use the existing app/SQLite owner and one bounded asynchronous import runner. The runner invokes the acquisition subsystem through its public value/effect ports and starts only fixed `git`, `gh` and `glab` commands with argument arrays. It is not a new service, remote worker, daemon or shell executor. Native async coordination and the managed registry are sufficient; no reactive-library dependency is selected.

SQLite stores job intent, phase/selection, revisions, durable receipts, invocation/process observations and result references. Every mutation uses authenticated domain ingress or a narrowly scoped private internal command grant from the same owner. A transaction ends before subprocess spawn, provider/Git I/O, artifact I/O, source verification or user selection. Waiting jobs do not hold transactions or the runner slot. One active import invocation protects process ownership; discussion and other authorized review commands use independent short transactions and remain usable.

The acquisition module has no database/UI access. Source preparation owns the acquisition-v1 verification/mapping boundary and mints an internal witness only from its trusted public acquisition call, not a caller's JSON or “verified” flag. Domain/storage owns immutable review admission, permissions, CAS and receipts. UI collects intent and renders committed queries; neither components nor stream operators implement job/admission policy.

## Identity and authority

| Identity | Meaning and boundary |
|---|---|
| commandId | One authenticated intent and canonical payload fingerprint. Same actor/payload retries return original receipt; changed payload conflicts. Job commands do not reuse question or admission IDs. |
| jobId | Durable user import request with owner actor and credential reference, canonical requested path, target mode and bounds. It survives browser/process restarts. No bearer token is stored in job data. |
| discoveryRevision | Versioned candidate set and issues. Explicit selection names a candidate from this exact set; stale/foreign selection rejects. |
| jobRevision | Orders job state/readback. It is not a review revision. Job receipts identify job scope and minimum job revision; successful admission additionally returns actual review revision/snapshotId. |
| invocationId | One claimed effect phase (discovery, acquisition or explicitly required re-verification), distinct from commandId/jobId. Persist before any subprocess. Retries of an unknown invocation never get a new ID automatically. |
| ownerRunId / generation | Exact current app owner and runner claim. The exclusive data-root/runtime lock remains required. Restart advances runner generation; prior in-memory grants cannot apply late results. |
| process observation | Invocation plus ordinal, fixed executable role, requested/spawn-observed/exit-observed state, owned PID/start evidence, exit/signal and bounded reason. Do not persist credential-bearing argv, provider stderr or token values. |
| artifactId | Owner-generated identifier bound to job/invocation, content digest/byte length, schema/identity scheme and retained result. It is not an arbitrary filesystem path or permission to open a supplied URL. |
| admissionCommandId | Stable derived identity for this job/result/target admission, retained through crash/readback. Initial create and continuation are explicit distinct modes. New explicit conflict resolution uses a new command, never alters an old payload. |

Only the server-derived local owner (or retained valid user credential) may request/discover/select/cancel/admit source. Existing agent attachments can read authorized source and reply under their generation; bootstrap and agent credentials cannot import arbitrary filesystem paths or enlarge their review scope. Import grants no new attachment and never forks/resumes a substitute session. Apply-time checks use the request's actual active owner credential reference and current target authorization; recorded actor strings alone do not authorize a late result.

The runner obtains a nonserialized internal grant bound to job, invocation, phase, generation and permitted result transitions. It can report only that invocation's observations/result; it cannot issue general user commands or write another review. External `/api/commands` callers cannot forge this grant. No new worker HTTP endpoint, bearer credential in an artifact or global session setting is needed. Same-OS-owner trust is retained; this is not remote attestation.

## Durable lifecycle

States and observations remain separate: command accepted is not a process start, a successful CLI exit is not a complete acquisition result, and a prepared result is not an admitted snapshot.

| State / transition | Required semantics |
|---|---|
| Request → queued discovery | Atomic job creation and receipt; validate owner/path shape/bounds. Resolve real worktree via the trusted acquisition port, not by changing cwd/branch globally. |
| Claim → discovering | Atomic CAS from eligible queued state, allocate invocation and private grant, persist launch intent; release transaction before effects. Persist each subprocess request before spawning and record observed start/exit independently. |
| Discovery → choice required / unavailable / acquiring | Retain exact candidates/issues/revision. Multiple or incomplete routes require explicit selection. No candidate produces a truthful unavailable/no-match result. A fully unique result pins that candidate before automatic acquisition. |
| Selection → queued acquisition | User command names candidate identity plus discoveryRevision and target choice. Validate membership and authorization; no arbitrary candidate JSON becomes trusted metadata. Import refreshes provider identity and rejects drift as stale rather than importing a different head. |
| Acquisition running → result ready | Trusted source-preparation call invokes reviewed acquisition public port and validates full result/schema/identity; all owned effects have observed completion. Atomically publish a complete owned result artifact, then commit its reference and result receipt. An existing provider result may have unsupported/missing entries; that differs from a failed whole import. |
| Result ready → admitted | After artifact verification and an in-memory witness, use one atomic admission transaction for source/review changes, admission receipt and job disposition. Result references and source remain exact. Emit committed view updates only after commit; no agent wake. |
| Admission conflict | Retain result and typed reason (current snapshot, review identity, source/metadata conflict or limit); no partial history mutation. Offer explicit inspection/target reconciliation. No automatic retarget to the new current snapshot. |
| Definitive unavailable/failed | Record actual reason, phase and whether any process ran. A missing tool before spawn is different from a timeout/unknown launch. An explicit new request may retry after process quiescence; the old job/history remains. |
| Cancel requested | Durable owner command. Before claim/selection it cancels without launch. During an owned invocation stop new subcommands, request termination only of verified owned processes/groups, await evidence and record confirmed cancelled or unknown. |
| Unknown | Startup/crash/uncertain acknowledgement cannot establish whether effects ran or stopped. Retain original invocation/process evidence, quarantine it from replay and reconcile safely. Elapsed timeout or PID absence alone cannot reconstruct a missing result. |

The owner tracks child handles for normal cancellation and records process start identity for recovery. Never kill a reused/unverified PID or a process group belonging to another runtime. Confirm termination using owned process/group observations appropriate to the supported host; signal delivery alone is not cancellation. If termination cannot be established, show unknown and retain evidence. A cancellation/admission race is serialized: if cancel is committed first, no later source admission; if admission committed first, cancel reports already completed and does not delete source/history.

On restart, unclaimed queued work may be claimed once. Claimed work without definitive outcome becomes unknown; do not invoke acquisition/discovery again automatically. A persisted complete result with a matching admission receipt is read back without relaunch. A result-ready artifact lacking an admission receipt is verified before continuation. Because witnesses are in-memory, restart requires a new **explicit** owner re-verification action using a separately journaled invocation against the same pinned candidate and reviewed acquisition algorithm; it cannot replay an unknown original invocation. Provider drift during that re-verification rejects as stale and preserves the old result. No fabricated historical provider response is supplied to make verification pass.

A new job after an unknown one is an explicit user action, never an automatic retry. The owner first establishes that the old invocation is no longer running; otherwise it still occupies the one active effect slot. Existing reviews/comments remain usable. This conservative limitation is acceptable for the first single-host implementation and must be visible in diagnostics and recovery guidance.

## Public operations: existing versus new

Existing 02B ports are `store.command` for review writes, `AddSnapshot` with expectedCurrentSnapshotId, `store.review` with optional historical snapshot selection, user-only review listing, and public `source-preparation` manual verification/witness checks. These ports have bounded independent engineering and actual own-PR continuation/navigation acceptance; full native/human/480p acceptance remains separate. `store.prepare` remains bounded setup/recovery, not authenticated product import ingress.

The candidate implements RequestImport, ChooseImportCandidate, CancelImport, explicit ReverifyImportResult and AdmitImportResult, with the strict owner command shapes below. Authorized job queries return the active credential's jobs and their revisions. These are candidate interfaces, not final slice acceptance. Internal claim/process/discovery/result/admission commands use the same store owner and durable receipt/transaction policy through the private execution grant.

Initial import uses the verified review-creation transition through private job admission, atomically creating review/source/receipt and marking the job admitted. There is no raw provider-manifest HTTP CreateReview command; the owner RequestImport lifecycle and its live verification witness authorize creation. Reserve its generated reviewId once the target choice is fixed. Repeated exact admission returns its receipt; it must not call setup `prepare` from HTTP. Before creating, check stable provider/host/target-project/change identity in the same transaction: if an existing review appeared, return an explicit existing-review conflict/choice instead of silently creating a duplicate or overwriting discussion. Legacy duplicate reviews are preserved and listed for explicit selection; do not migrate/deduplicate them behind the user.

Continuation uses AddSnapshot semantics through the same domain transition and witness boundary, extended to `acquisition_v1`. Pin reviewId and expectedCurrentSnapshotId before acquisition. Preserve exact retained-snapshot idempotency without rewind, source conflict rejection, membership checks and old question/reply/source queries. If current changed, retain the result and require an explicit new admission command with the inspected expected current; source verification must remain valid. Exact already-retained snapshots can be acknowledged without fresh provider effects, as in 02B.

Do not implement product creation by direct SQL from acquisition or a second writable SQLite connection. The owning store may factor common transaction helpers so review admission, job completion and their receipts commit together without nested transactions. Commands and queries retain different job/review revision scopes.

## Acquisition-v1 identity and verified admission

Preserve the reviewed provider import algorithm rather than recomputing a generic sorted JSON hash. It is SHA-256 over compact UTF-8 JSON constructed in this order: provider, host, targetProject, sourceProject, number, baseSha, headSha, sources, changedFiles. The source array and changed-file/hunk/disposition order are those produced by the reviewed acquisition adapter, not transport object property order. Each disposition is constructed as side, path, state, reason, objectId; each hunk as id, oldStart, oldLines, newStart, newLines. A hunk ID is SHA-256 of the old path string, NUL, new path string, NUL and exact matched zero-context hunk header; an absent path contributes the literal string `null`. Counts are retained outside the snapshot digest; `counts.bytes` counts acquired blob bytes before decoding/coverage rejection, not only selectable text bytes. Recompute or verify those meanings through the public reviewed acquisition port, not an independent competing hash implementation. Source fields are side, path, content, hash, objectId, lineCount; file entries are status, oldPath, newPath, oldMode, newMode, dispositions, hunks, coverage. Retain all source/object/path/mode/side/hunk fields and exact counts. Do not transform a provider value into the manual hash recipe.

Map top-level review snapshot fields from the verified candidate (target project as repository, candidate URL/number/base/head/title), retain the complete candidate plus original sources/changedFiles/counts and acquisition snapshotId. Provider state/title/branch observations are retained even where not in the identity digest. Same snapshot ID with a different canonical retained manifest remains an explicit snapshot conflict; do not silently refresh historical metadata or alter the ID to avoid it. A job can retain the differing observation for inspection.

The candidate public source-preparation acquisition adapter is implemented. It accepts trusted job inputs/effects, calls `source-acquisition/public.ts`, validates content/provenance/recipe, and returns the exact mapped snapshot plus a nonserialized witness bound to job/review/exact canonical manifest. Its constructor stays private. Raw HTTP snapshots, artifact JSON, worker status strings, or schema validity alone cannot mint it. No acquisition internals are imported into storage; the mapper consumes only public immutable values. A same-owner returned value from the trusted acquisition call is distinct from untrusted deserialized input. On recovery, re-verification follows the explicit lifecycle above before a fresh witness is issued.

Maintain reviewed acquisition effect safeguards: no shell, branch switch, source execution, install hooks, external diffs/textconv or automatic fetch. Disable lazy object retrieval, replace objects, inherited Git overrides, hooks/fsmonitor and nonliteral pathspec interpretation. Pin attribute/diff/order behavior; missing objects remain missing. Existing provider clients may perform their supported authenticated API reads, but repository configuration must not choose executable helpers to acquire absent source. Another Git version missing required flags returns unavailable; never retry with weaker flags. The import worker's cancellable effect adapter must preserve these properties when replacing the existing noncancellable Node runner.

### Representation without loss

Current 02B manual schema requires nonempty content, positive line counts, one or more sources and at most 512 source entries. Provider acquisition legitimately returns zero-line empty blobs, all-unsupported manifests with no selectable text, and up to two source sides for each of 512 changed paths. Slice03 must explicitly extend provider-specific admission to support empty strings with lineCount zero, zero selectable sources and at most 1,024 source entries. Keep empty prepared blobs and their object/hash identity; no invented line 1 or empty opposite side for additions/deletions. An all-binary/unsupported PR still has a useful complete ledger and can be reviewed, but no source-span question can target absent text.

Legacy/manual checks and IDs stay unchanged. Additive provider schema validation permits only these documented cases, still checks strict bytes/hash, source-key consistency, candidate consistency, path containment, disposition/count/hunk coherence and source-side bounds. UI comparisons and selection must handle empty/absent/unsupported sides without crashing or inventing anchors. Raw provider hunks, rather than the bootstrap line comparator, are the authoritative imported coverage spans; semantic analysis is still not performed.

## Envelope, artifacts and storage bounds

The public encoded command envelope remains at most 8 MiB including JSON metadata; existing question/reply bounds are unchanged. Acquisition defaults remain 512 changed paths, 1 MiB per blob, 8 MiB accumulated blob bytes, 4,096 hunks and 1 MiB inventory output. Raw content bytes, encoded result bytes and displayed/selectable bytes are different measures. JSON escaping can exceed either transport or artifact bounds even when raw acquisition content is within budget.

Use a small internal result reference instead of posting full source through the command envelope. Result artifacts have a separate **16 MiB encoded UTF-8 limit**, including metadata; results over it fail explicitly as result-too-large with no truncation or changed identity. Provider admissions also enforce a **64 MiB total encoded retained-source budget per review**; existing legacy data is retained, and exceeding the budget rejects only the new admission. These initial limits are declared scope, not measured scalability claims. Never delete old snapshots automatically to admit a new one.

Store artifacts only beneath the existing private external runtime data root in owner-generated import-job/invocation directories. Commands carry artifactId/digest/length, never arbitrary path. The owner maps IDs to its registry, rejects traversal/absolute paths/symlinks and verifies real containment, exclusive ownership and regular-file type. Write an exclusive mode-0600 temporary file, finish/hash/fsync it, publish without replacement using a same-directory hard link to the generated final name, unlink the temporary name and fsync the directory, then persist the matching reference. Link publication gives atomic appearance without rename’s overwrite behavior. Do not log source, remote credentials or bearer tokens. On read, open without following symlinks, bound bytes and use the same file descriptor for type/length/hash/content checks before parsing. A stored digest mismatch or observed replacement is a verification failure, not authority to reread another file. Reject unsafe existing directories rather than chmod them. Public Node24 filesystem APIs lack directory-descriptor-relative open/rename; the supported boundary is the existing private0700 single-owner root with pre/post stable-parent, no-symlink, regular-file, no-follow and same-file-descriptor integrity checks. It does not establish hostile same-UID namespace isolation against an adversary swapping parent directories. No native helper/dependency or persisted-inode attestation is introduced; restart validates registered reference/binding and current content integrity.

Artifact I/O, JSON parsing, source consistency checks and witness creation finish before admission transaction. Small result-reference validation does not lift source/schema limits. A failed artifact write leaves no admitted review. An orphan temp/final file is not a completed job; retain/reconcile by job identity rather than age, and do not guess that it was consumed. A committed admitted snapshot is authoritative even if an optional result export later disappears. Cleanup retains artifacts needed by pending/unknown/conflicted jobs; delete only task-owned disposable copies after verified knowledge/recovery reconciliation.

## Execution bounds and reactive behavior

Default single owner permits one active effect invocation and eight queued/choice/result-ready jobs; excess requests return a typed capacity result without losing accepted work. Each phase has a120-second total deadline. Discovery allows at most256 subprocess launches; acquisition and explicit re-verification allow at most4096 and acquisition's per-command timeout/output limits (provider calls up to 15 seconds; discovery Git reads up to five seconds). The deadline stops new subcommands and requests owned termination; it does not itself prove cancelled/failed. Waiting for explicit choice does not consume a live process slot. Scope/limit changes require a documented contract revision, not hidden retries or parallel spawns.

Declare public routes for import-request-committed → runner eligibility, job-committed → authorized job view and review-admitted → review view. Coalesce replaceable progress views only; accepted intents/results/receipts are durable. Remount/reconnect must not claim another invocation. Revoked/disposed UI subscriptions ignore late emissions; runner ownership is gateway/application lifetime, not React lifetime. Job completion does not enqueue an agent turn in this slice; subscribed job-terminal enrichment belongs to slice08.

## Complete ledger and graph presentation

Show provider/project/change identity, actual comparison base/head and snapshot identity; each changed path has its status, old/new path/modes, existing-side dispositions, supported hunks or explicit unsupported reason. A raw hunk has one primary ledger identity even if referenced by several graph/context views. Retain added/deleted/renamed/copied/type-changed and metadata-only/empty cases. Entire inventory failure is an unavailable import, never a shortened “complete” ledger.

Keep complete changed-file inventory, selected input, actually prepared/context source and analyzed relationships distinct. Basic slice03 imports all changed paths within declared bounds and does not require the separate unchanged-context loader. File/hunk/contains/comparison bootstrap edges remain source structure; imported material without analyzed document references says not analyzed. The manual first-120-link cap is not a complete unresolved-call/link ledger. No call graph, confirmed semantic leaf or repository test execution is claimed.

Keep all bounded ledger facts accessible while showing a readable chosen file/span/owner pair, with explicit navigation to remaining entries. Graph focus cannot retarget source selection or drafts. An import completing in the background does not move a review/history selection or replace the source behind a pending question; opening/selecting the new result is explicit.

## Verification, rationale and knowledge

Choose this design because an existing single owner already provides atomic review commands and private runtime ownership. One asynchronous runner and durable journal are sufficient for a useful bounded import; a distributed queue, worker service, generic workflow engine or new authentication layer would add scope without solving the immediate task. An artifact reference avoids weakening the transport limit or silently cutting source. Existing setup prepare is retained for recovery, while product creation gains actual authorization/receipt semantics.

Required evidence includes real-process faults around request/claim/spawn/result/admission, cancellation and restart without replay; exact ID/metadata/empty/unsupported preservation; artifact tamper/path/size rejection; comments progressing during a real import; actual React path-choice-ledger-history journey and fresh graph-first own-PR critique. Unit fixtures and GitHub success never establish live GitLab/native/human acceptance. The owning slice records candidate/target and actual results; these are verification requirements, with exact executed evidence and outstanding gates recorded in the owning slice.

At milestone acceptance, reflect on actual structure, update learned decisions/limits here and audit whole-current-product rebuild readiness from durable docs only under [round reflection](../../rules/round-reflection.md). A docs audit does not claim an actual rebuild. The single-owner access correction removes manual login/passkeys; preserve pilot/data/session/routes and do not reopen native CLI investigation for this slice.


## Integration derivation decisions

The bounded implementation uses domain-owned import intent/state policy, the existing storage owner for job/review/receipt atomicity, and an import-jobs coordinator for asynchronous acquisition/process effects. Artifact I/O is an independent public boundary returning only a strict registered reference and unknown parsed JSON, never an admission witness. Its reference contains artifactId, jobId, invocationId, digest, bytes and schema import-result-v1; digest/length cover the complete compact encoded envelope (schema, artifactId, jobId, invocationId, unchanged acquisition value). Expected job/invocation bindings come from stored owner state, not the request’s arbitrary path.

New requests declare new-review or explicit same-review continuation intent. Candidate choices name an ID from a committed discoveryRevision; target choice is fixed before acquisition. A unique candidate with no existing matching review can proceed to creation automatically. Existing matching reviews require explicit selection/continuation, including legacy duplicate-review choices; a concurrent later identity collision is retained as a conflict. An explicit AdmitImportResult owner action can inspect a retained result and supply a new target/expected-current, creating a new admission attempt identity instead of altering a rejected receipt. Missing in-memory verification after restart requires explicit ReverifyImportResult and a separately journaled provider invocation, not trust in the artifact.

### Repeated identical copy-source occurrences

Reviewed acquisition-v1 can repeat a source occurrence when one base blob participates in both a modified original and a copied file. Preserve its EXACT source array/order/digest, prepared-side counts and byte accounting. Repeated (side,path) keys are admissible only when the full canonical source value (including content/hash/object ID/line count and its candidate-bound commit provenance) is identical. Conflicting values reject before admission. Manual preparation retains strict no-duplicate rules. Derive a separate unique lookup/render index for unambiguous anchors; never deduplicate the retained provider manifest or call occurrence counts unique files. Each primary file/hunk ledger still retains its own identity and copied-path relationship.

A normative real-Git case modifies a.txt while copying its original content to b.txt. The ordered ledger is modified a.txt→a.txt then copied a.txt→b.txt; ordered sources are base a.txt, head a.txt, base a.txt, head b.txt. PreparedSides is4 although there are three unique source keys. Deduplicating that array changes the reviewed identity and is incompatible. ## Current design reflection

Actual implementation inspection supports retaining one SQLite owner and immutable aggregate sources, with small private artifacts bridging async effects to admission. A second worker database or provider JSON flag would split atomicity or trust. The identity lookup is a deliberate derived index so collision checks do not decode every historical source body. Content verification, budgets and request hashing stay outside the transaction; authoritative membership/current checks and writes stay inside. Native async effects plus managed routes satisfy the bounded lifecycle without another library/service. Readable focused graph views sit over the full immutable ledger; future context/relations must preserve that invariant instead of fitting all facts onto a miniature canvas.

The React panel is pure presentation over application-supplied action availability; subscriptions, stable unknown-request retry and effect scheduling remain outside it. The import-request-to-runner and verified-result-to-admission registry routes belong to the runner, job-committed-to-authorized-view belongs to the import bridge, and the existing review-committed-to-view route projects admitted history without moving private selection. React remount reads status rather than claiming jobs. Source comparison focus is private view state; saved anchors retain exact snapshot/side/path/lines, including shared copy bases, rather than a persistent ledger-view selection. Reopening a shared source may require explicitly choosing its comparison again.

These are delivered bounded03 design/compatibility facts. Independent engineering, representative actual own-PR import/continuation and cumulative docs-only sufficiency have separate identity-bound receipts; they do not establish every schedule, maximum-size performance or a successful rebuild. No target program/tests execute; context/analysis04, live GitLab, automatic native turn/catalog, Claude and unfamiliar-human acceptance remain outside this evidence.


A retained legacy setup value whose URL cannot establish a host remains readable but is not entered into the provider identity lookup. The index must not invent a host or let such a value claim provider membership. This preserves earlier controlled/setup compatibility without treating an invalid URL as acquisition provenance.


## Corrected bounded integration decisions

The initial256-launch import ceiling rejected the actual49-path PR23 at256 observed exits despite a complete public acquisition requiring261 Git and2 gh commands. The import-only ceiling is now4096, retaining discovery256, total120-second phase deadline, one active invocation, queue8, per-command/source/artifact bounds and all fixed-executable/no-target-execution protections. This is a bounded policy correction, not a new Git algorithm or source identity. A calculated worst-case successful acquisition uses5 Git setup calls (type+commit for each pin and one raw inventory), at most3 reads per1024 existing sides, at most1 patch per512 paths and up to3 provider refresh calls:5+3072+512+3=3592. GitHub’s2 provider calls give3591; GitLab’s3 give3592. Unsupported routes can stop earlier. Observed PR23 used5+3×69+49=261 Git calls plus2 gh; it does not prove worst-case runtime performance. An injected owner test limit may only lower these ceilings, never enlarge them or arrive through HTTP/environment.

Retained-source quota has one exact representation: sum UTF8 byte lengths of compact JSON.stringify(snapshot.sources) for every retained snapshot, preserving source occurrence/array order, source member names/values and ordinary JSON escaping. An empty source array costs2 bytes. This is the encoded source-array quota, not a whole review/DB/ledger quota and not raw content bytes. An exact boundary is allowed; one byte over rejects only the new admission. Exact already-retained acknowledgements add no second charge. Preserve over-budget legacy/history records and all prior IDs/current/question/credential/receipt state; no eviction or re-encoding to fit. Validation/source sizing occurs outside the effectful transaction; authoritative retained state and current CAS still determine atomic apply. Owner-only test constructors may lower the byte limit for exact boundary cases, not raise the64MiB product maximum. The store constructor accepts an optional importLimits object with maxLaunches (integer1–4096) and maxRetainedSourceBytes (integer1–67108864); omitted values use the product maxima. The launch override is additionally capped at256 for discovery. These options are internal test/control inputs, absent from HTTP and environment configuration; invalid values reject initialization.

In-pane line selection preserves the currently displayed copy/rename comparison when the chosen source belongs to that comparison. It changes only the immutable anchor’s selected line range; it does not drop the private comparison key and substitute another After path. External saved-anchor reopening may still require choosing a shared comparison again. No comparison key is added to persisted question anchors or source hashes.

The import bridge’s reads and command publications belong to a credential/generation and connection lifetime. Explicit login starts a new generation, clears the previous active view/intent recovery and does not let an old request publish jobs/errors or clear a newer pending command. A command already sent may still commit server-side; this is not rollback or permission to resubmit it as a new credential. Disposal invalidates/aborts only owned reads; reconnect rereads authorized state and old completions remain fenced. Regular polling does not replace an explicit login/readback read or acquire source. Active-connection teardown is idempotent and cannot invalidate a newer connection. A command dispatched before teardown may have committed: disposal keeps its unchanged-credential retry intent but fences late publication; reconnect rereads authorized state and exact retry keeps the same command ID. Explicit login, even to the same token, deliberately starts a new credential generation and clears prior scoped intent recovery; this does not undo any server receipt.

Exact provider candidate/value/enums/nulls/ordering and complete hash-input data are maintained in [acquisition compatibility](acquisition-compatibility.md). This supersedes references to an old adapter as the sole definition of hash-bearing fields.

## Import-job-v1 recovery reader details

Candidate and ordered candidates use acquisition-compatibility.md; candidate is null before a selection. Target, artifact and admission are explicit null until present, not omitted. Optional invocation.artifact and process observation fields remain absent until observed. Admission is an ImportReceipt with the exact body defined above, not a review Receipt/cursor.

Discovery is initially null. A committed discovery contains canonicalWorktree (string/null), branch (string/null), upstream (string/null), remotes (ordered host/project objects), candidates (ordered complete provider candidates), issues (ordered reason plus optional provider/host), kind and reason. Kind is none/unique/ambiguous/unavailable; reason is resolved/no_match/detached/incomplete. Process startIdentity is an opaque observed identity string: trimmed stdout of local /bin/ps requested for that pid with lstart and pgid columns, retaining internal whitespace. On the supported Unix host it combines the process start display and group ID. It is compared to a fresh identical observation before signaling, not parsed into source or reconstituted from pid alone. Fast-exited children may have pid but no observed startIdentity; that absence never authorizes a kill. Group absence can establish quiescence; missing launch acknowledgement cannot establish a replacement process to signal.

## Review-informed rebuild and verified limits

Actual structure still favors one authoritative SQLite owner, one bounded asynchronous runner, immutable acquisition values and private proof-bound admission. Rebuilding now should retain those boundaries and the independently verifiable artifact port; a new daemon, duplicated source store or browser-owned import policy would add competing authority. Generation/connection/request ownership belongs at reactive effect boundaries; selection/comparison/draft stays private, and imported current source never moves historical discussion. The exact existing source/receipt identity adapters remain compatibility boundaries rather than opportunities to normalize retained values.

Representative live GitHub import/continuation and controlled lifecycle/fault checks support this bounded design. They do not establish worst-case120-second performance, every process schedule, live GitLab availability or native/human acceptance. Actual React lifecycle fixtures can measure managed-route diagnostics separately from process shutdown; an exited runtime alone is not a route-count measurement.

Independent graph-first investigation found readable complete inventory and precise source routing useful, but structural containment/pairing and repeated header excerpts did not explain the lifecycle, its safeguards or rationale. Opening dense physical source still required manual synthesis across coordinator, storage, preparation and application boundaries. Successors should preserve the complete ledger and exact source identity while preparing defensible responsibility/neighbor evidence and meaningful declaration/body context; structural counts or a static call alone cannot stand in for the business story. This is a learned product gap, not evidence that caller/story preparation already exists.

Persisting a cited reply is separate from answering the question. A generic identity-continuity fixture can verify storage, evidence links and history while failing to explain the user's actual concern. Evaluate relevance, reasoning and source sufficiency independently; Notified records a delivery attempt outcome, not receipt/consumption or answer quality. Keep source-corrected agent critique distinct from unfamiliar-human comprehension and measured productivity.

## Journal-loss quiescence correction (05E)

A terminal journal label is a leader observation, not proof that no process was spawned. If persisting `started` fails after a durable request, the child may already own live descendants. Every later terminal observation must repeat the actual observed pid and startIdentity when available, even when the earlier start write failed. Journal uncertainty remains sticky in the adapter; retaining identity permits safe read-only reconciliation, not immediate success or signaling an unverified group.

Add optional private process field `spawnDisposition: not_spawned` only for a definitive spawn-error event before any start was observed and with no child PID. This is additive to existing records; absence means no such proof. Reject contradictory not_spawned observations (started state, observed pid/startIdentity or previously started/pid-bearing journal). A legacy exited record without pid and without that explicit proof remains unresolved. Do not infer not_spawned from its reason string, exit code, missing identity or omitted field. Existing receipts, admitted results and source/history remain unchanged.

A shared pure process-journal eligibility predicate admits read-only reconciliation only for (a) started/exited with a positive safe observed PID, requiring a fresh absent owned-group observation, or (b) exited with explicit not_spawned and no contradictory identity. Requested-only and ambiguous missing-PID rows retain the unknown barrier. Both import and semantic coordinators use this rule; storage independently refuses confirmQuiescent when any retained process lacks this minimum evidence. An empty journal may settle only under the existing durable-request-before-spawn contract, which proves no instrumented effect was launched. Earlier ambiguous processes cannot be hidden by later complete observations.

Reconciliation never signals a missing/reused/unverified identity. A live group keeps the shared lease, even when its leader exited. Once positive group absence is observed, stopped effects can be recorded without inventing a successful result or replaying the interrupted invocation. Failed terminal journal persistence leaves the original requested/started record and uncertainty intact. Current owner/epoch fences remain mandatory for every store mutation; cancellation/shutdown still settle only the actual owned handles within existing limits.

The correction's shared domain/public function is `processQuiescenceEligible(record)`, where the record contains state and optional pid/startIdentity/spawnDisposition. It performs no OS effect and rejects unknown spawn-disposition values. `import-jobs/public.processQuiescent(record)` applies that minimum rule and, for an observed PID, performs the existing read-only group-existence probe. Both coordinators call it; both stores recheck minimum eligibility before confirming an unknown invocation. Storage still relies on its private current owner for the fresh group-absence observation and does not execute an OS probe inside a transaction. `not_spawned` is accepted only on an exited observation replacing a requested row with no prior observed PID/startIdentity. No persisted schema rewrite is required; old ambiguous records remain unknown instead of being silently upgraded.

### Availability when process identity is permanently missing

A permanently requested-only journal, or a legacy exited record without trustworthy PID/nonlaunch evidence, can keep the shared import/analysis lane blocked indefinitely. Elapsed time, cancellation, supersession, restart, a closed gateway or an apparent retry action do not supply missing evidence and do not authorize releasing that obligation. The delivered product has no public UI, CLI or MCP force-clear or general repair workflow for this condition. Retained reviews, source and comments are separate from the execution lane and can remain usable while new resource-consuming work cannot claim it; this is not a guarantee against arbitrary storage/OS failure.

Supported reconciliation relies only on the existing recognized write-ahead/no-launch cases or trustworthy private owner observations: a later genuine terminal observation may retain the original PID/start identity, after which fresh owned-group absence can permit settlement under the current owner/epoch. An empty journal is meaningful only under the durable-request-before-spawn contract; explicit not_spawned must satisfy its definitive pre-start evidence rules. If such evidence cannot be obtained, the unknown barrier remains. Do not manufacture an observation, guess a PID, reset the database or imply a delivered recovery feature. Confirmed stopped effects permit the appropriate interrupted disposition; they never establish that a lost import/analysis result succeeded or replay the interrupted invocation.

## Single-owner access correction

The public browser imports bridge opens without credentials through `open()` and sends no Authorization header. Lower-level `login(token)` remains a programmatic compatibility seam, never a required product flow. Trusted local-owner storage access lists and manages every retained job with actorId=local-user, including legacy credential-reference jobs; it does not rewrite their reference, credential rows or receipt identity. Explicit credential calls retain their existing reference checks. New owner jobs persist local-owner:v1, recognized by the runner after restart without issuing a credential. All other job/effect/admission fences remain unchanged.

files.after: # Persisted data and legacy identity compatibility **Contract:** Documentation version 1. These names describe delivered formats; they are not new persisted schema/version fields. **Parents:** [Review contracts](contracts.md), [continuation and preparation](evolution.md), [additive import job/identity formats](import-jobs.md#persisted-job-representation-and-public-ports) Rebuilding the current product includes opening a copy of its supported earlier SQLite store, not merely inventing equivalent fresh data. Preserve source IDs, saved discussion, capabilities, receipts, inbox cursors and notification uncertainty. Never repair incompatibility by resetting data or generating replacement source/participant identities. ## SQLite aggregate formats The delivered files use SQLite user_version 0 with JSON text records; there is no numeric application schema discriminator. The following physical tables and column names are compatibility facts. Identity keys and JSON bodies are text; added revision/byte columns described below are integers. JSON bodies use the member names below. Extra retained JSON members survive an additive migration and are not automatically interpreted as new authority. | Table / key | Other columns and meaning | |---|---| | reviews / id | body: review aggregate. id equals body.reviewId. | | receipts / id | actor, fingerprint, body. id is commandId; actor is the authenticated actorId, fingerprint is the versioned SHA-256 representation below, body is the immutable receipt. | | credentials / hash | body: principal JSON. hash is lowercase SHA-256 hex of the UTF-8 bearer token, never the plaintext token. Existing token/verifier pairs remain unchanged. | | challenges / id | body: reviewId, host, sessionId, connectionId, owner (actorId), proofHash (SHA-256 UTF-8 proof), expiry (Unix milliseconds), consumed (boolean). One-use/expiry/connection checks survive migration. | | preparation_inputs / review_id | body: validated original manual specification, separate from history. review_id references reviews.id. This table/row may be absent in earlier stores; create the empty table without changing earlier records. | Pre-history review bodies contain reviewId, snapshot, revision, attachment (object or null), questions, replies, inbox and attempts. Current bodies additionally retain snapshots (ordered immutable snapshot array) and currentSnapshotId. The stored snapshot compatibility member follows current after a new admission. Public queries substitute the selected snapshot and derive snapshotSummaries; summaries are not a second authoritative source store. Missing optional parentQuestionId or reply.snapshotId remains absent, not null/default-generated. | Aggregate value | Persisted members / interpretation | |---|---| | Snapshot / source | Snapshot: snapshotId, repository, prUrl, prNumber, baseSha, headSha, sources; optional title, changedFiles, documentReferences. Source: path, side, content, lineCount, hash. The newer optional provider/object/mode/hunk/count fields are defined in evolution knowledge and must be preserved if present; manual-v1 does not fabricate them. | | Attachment | attachmentId, actorId, host (`codex` or `claude`), sessionId, connectionId, generation, active. Preserve the entire binding; source addition does not replace it. | | Question | questionId, anchor, text, actorId, revision, createdAt (UTC string), working (boolean); newer optional parentQuestionId. Anchor members are snapshotId, side (`base` or `head`), path, startLine, endLine, one-based inclusive. | | Reply | replyId, questionId, body, evidence (anchor array), limitations, actorId, attachmentId, generation, revision; newer optional snapshotId. For legacy replies without it, the question's anchor supplies snapshot identity; do not rewrite their evidence. | | Inbox item | eventId, questionId, attachmentId, generation, cursor, read (boolean). Array order, cursor/read state and addressed event IDs remain intact. | | Attempt | invocationId, eventIds (ordered array), attachmentId, generation, state (`requested`, `notifying`, `notified`, `unknown`, `failed`), reason. Migration never starts/replays an attempt. Separate runtime recovery changes a surviving notifying claim to unknown while retaining its identity. | | Receipt body | commandId, actorId, state (`applied` or `rejected`), revision, cursor, result (opaque result object), optional error. Preserve body and actor/fingerprint columns, including rejected outcomes. | Credential body discrimination is by kind: user has actorId (issued local owner is `local-user`); agent has actorId, reviewId, attachmentId, generation; bootstrap has actorId, host, sessionId, connectionId, corroborated (boolean). The issuer generates 32 random bytes represented as 64 lowercase hex characters for tokens; imported existing tokens need not be regenerated. Authentication derives the principal from the verifier row and rechecks current attachment/generation for agent access. A stored bootstrap claim is not general source access. Provider/import additions retain their exact physical/job/receipt/reference formats in import-jobs.md; they add tables and a derived review identity lookup without rewriting these legacy rows. The migration discriminator is missing history members, not an absent version number: use an existing snapshots array if present, otherwise the original snapshot as a one-element array; use existing currentSnapshotId if present, otherwise original snapshot.snapshotId. Require a nonempty array, unique snapshot IDs and a pointer found in that array. If either history member was absent, save the additive result. Preserve revision and every other aggregate value, array order, other table row and credential verifier. Perform all review conversions in one transaction; malformed JSON or failed history integrity aborts and rolls back earlier conversions. Reopen is idempotent. This is a compatibility reader for the described family, not a universal corrupt-store repair or future-version converter; unsupported structure must not be guessed/reset. Initialization may create missing declared tables; failure does not erase recoverable original bodies. For example, a legacy body with snapshot S, revision 6, question Q anchored to S and unknown attempt I becomes the same body plus snapshots=[S] and currentSnapshotId=S. Q, I, their cursor/generation, receipt rows and credential hashes remain unchanged. A malformed second review cannot leave the first review half-converted. After admitting T, current becomes T while S/Q/I remain retained. Repeated original setup verifies S against history and exports T, without rewinding current. Legacy local-user.json may contain a plaintext local bearer in its token member and older runtime.json may carry its reference. Preserve existing files, but current runtime startup neither reads nor creates them and new manifests omit that reference. The file is never public protocol output. source-input.json and snapshot.json are regenerable setup/current exports. Runtime/PID/lock and MCP launch files are local operational references, not a substitute for SQLite authority. Preserve them separately during owner-approved backup; never publish their credential contents. ## Manual source identity v1 Read original Git blob bytes with strict UTF-8 decoding, preserving a leading UTF-8 BOM as U+FEFF. Do not normalize Unicode, CRLF or trailing newline. Reject invalid UTF-8, NUL and empty selectable content. SHA-256 source hash uses the original decoded string re-encoded as UTF-8, lowercase hex. Split source lines only at LF; if content ends in LF, exclude exactly the final empty split element from lineCount. CR remains in its line. Thus `A\r\n` and `B\n` each have one line; `A\n\n` has two, and a lone LF is one empty selectable line. BOM contributes to hash/content. The presentation may display an empty line, but must not change stored bytes to compute identity. [Construction order](evolution.md#verified-preparation-and-identity-schemes) is normative. Compact JSON uses ordinary JSON string escaping, no indentation or terminal newline; omitted optional members are absent, never synthesized null. One-path identity has only baseSha, headSha, sources: no empty changedFiles/documentReferences arrays. Multi-path identity includes those arrays even when references are empty. Added oldPath and deleted newPath are explicitly null; there is no disposition or invented source for the absent side. Sources/dispositions follow literal Git inventory order with base before head; context appends in link encounter order. Manual status literals are modified, added, deleted, type_changed. The manifest uses repository `scottchu/pr-reviewer` and real matching project PR aliases, independently verified by owner orchestration; those aliases/title are not in the legacy hash but are compared as part of the verified manifest. Disposition members are side, path, state, reason. The exact hash-bearing reason vocabulary is stable compatibility data: | State / trigger | Exact reason | |---|---| | prepared explicit text | `verified Git blob` | | prepared context promoted from an unprepared changed side | `verified referenced Git blob` | | unprepared outside explicit selection | `outside explicit prepared paths` | | unsupported failed Git/object read | `source_unavailable: pinned Git object cannot be read` | | unsupported non-blob | `source_unavailable: selected path must be a blob` | | unsupported invalid UTF-8 | `source_unavailable: selected blob is not valid UTF-8` | | unsupported NUL content | `source_unavailable: binary content` | | unsupported empty text | `source_unavailable: empty content` | A reference always has destination, source, target, method, reason, in that order. Destination is the extracted literal link destination. source is its exact same-side link-line anchor. target is a resolved exact same-side heading/start anchor or null; method is always `inline_markdown_link`. Success has reason null. Failure has target null and the exact reason: one of the source-read reasons above, `external destination`, `unsupported or outside repository destination`, `outside repository destination`, `heading fragment unresolved`, `context source budget exhausted`, or `URI malformed` for invalid percent escapes. These legacy reason strings participate in identity; improving diagnostic wording requires a new scheme, not changing an old ID. Both source/target anchors use literal snapshotId `pending` during hashing and the computed ID in the final manifest. Target source already read before an unresolved heading remains in sources. Context-only sources have no invented changed-file row. Missing is representable for later acquisition, but manual-v1 represents failed explicitly selected reads as unsupported. ## Receipt fingerprint v1 Normalize a valid command before hashing: trim question text, or reply body/limitations, using ECMAScript string trim and enforce the existing UTF-8 limits. Keep commandId, reviewId and every supplied validated member, including anchor/snapshot IDs and optional parentQuestionId; do not add absent optional values. On normalization failure, fingerprint the original valid-envelope payload and store its rejected receipt. Recursively sort object member names using the delivered ECMAScript String.localeCompare ordering (current schemas use fixed ASCII member names), retain array order, then compact JSON-serialize and SHA-256 its UTF-8 bytes to lowercase hex. This canonical order differs deliberately from the manual source hash's construction order. Unknown/extra envelope fields reject before this protocol; arbitrary object-order input permutations do not change a valid fingerprint. Look up receipt by commandId. Same actor and exact fingerprint returns its original body without a new revision/mutation, even after migration or when source verification later becomes unavailable. Changed payload or actor returns command_conflict without replacing that receipt. Pairing receipts use ID `attach:` followed by challengeId and fingerprint the canonical object containing challengeId and connectionId; the challenge is still single-use, not a generic AddSnapshot/AskQuestion replay route. Actor/hash/body preservation is necessary for unchanged legacy retries. ## Normative compatibility vectors These small data vectors describe hashing, not real provider provenance. The source fixture has fixed comparison base `85c4cc5ef2b3ae02fe120ac19aca2815d86268d5`, head `54d0cd7ca8d89a01a6feb02709ecb8f2d3fff3b0`. Base a.txt is `A\r\n`, head is `B\n`. Base b.md is `# Before\n[missing](missing.md)\n`, head is `# After\n[missing](missing.md)\n`. Both files are modified, sorted a.txt then b.md, and missing.md is absent on both sides. String escapes here denote actual characters; there are no BOMs in these vectors. | Vector | Required result | |---|---| | Source a.txt/base | lineCount 1; hash `26ffd5886253906a36a7ea0f6e26056fc36472626cb4894bcb100a34dc69d1db` | | Source a.txt/head | lineCount 1; hash `c0cde77fa8fef97d476c10aad3d2d54fcc2f336140d073651c2dcccf1e379fd6` | | One-path a.txt | base then head sources, no ledger/reference members; snapshotId `3fe24971d42609a7e83ea4ad5c693f908b03ed543ef8d82d7b71ce98f6a98ccf` | | Multi-path selecting only b.md | Sources b.md base/hash `343a3b6df93d6dbc620489c169bfaed2becf17b17c3cb8eeff6a4984ae6e82fd`, head/hash `c54a0cfda28c20ff85efb42f7ba22cd15f2561f61840493bf84b7f950a676a1e`, both lineCount 2. This is protocol data, not application implementation. New identity schemes must preserve or explicitly adapt these vectors without rewriting retained IDs. ## Manual Markdown reference identity v1 Reference recognition is a bounded delivered grammar, not CommonMark. These details determine retained source membership, reference anchors/reasons and therefore manual-v1 IDs. A replacement parser must reproduce this scheme or use a new version; it cannot silently enrich old manifests during verification. - Analyze only directly selected source paths ending in lowercase `.md`, in their existing source order; context added by links is not recursively analyzed. Split at LF, retaining the original one-based line number. A recognized link's source anchor spans that whole line (start=end), not character offsets. The global first-120 budget and source-object limits remain unchanged. - Exclude blockquote lines (up to three initial spaces then `>`), and lines indented by four spaces or a tab. Repeated blockquote prefixes are stripped only to recognize fence structure; quoted content is still excluded. A fence opener permits up to three spaces, an optional list marker (`-`, `+`, `*`, or decimal digits followed by `.`/`)`, then one space), and at least three identical backticks or tildes. Backtick openers cannot contain another backtick after the opening run. A closer has up to three spaces, the same marker repeated at least the opening length, then whitespace only, with matching quoted/unquoted context. All fence contents are excluded; list prefixes are not accepted on closing fences. - Outside excluded lines, a backslash and following UTF-16 code unit are treated as escaped text and cannot create syntax. Backtick runs suppress inline content until a run of exactly that opening length; this state can continue across lines and resets at a recognized fence opener. This conservative scanner does not implement all Markdown containers or emphasis rules. - Recognize `[label](destination)` with no whitespace between closing bracket and opening parenthesis: label is nonempty and contains no closing bracket, destination is nonempty and contains neither whitespace nor closing parenthesis. An immediately preceding `!` excludes images. A destination may be followed by whitespace and one double-quoted title before closing parenthesis; the title is not part of destination. No reference-style links, HTML links or single-quoted titles are interpreted. Angle brackets are not unwrapped; they remain literal path characters if encountered. Unsupported forms produce no attempted reference, rather than a fabricated unresolved record. - A URI scheme (letter first, then letters/digits/plus/dot/hyphen before colon) or leading `//` yields external destination. Otherwise split at the first literal `#`, then percent-decode path and fragment separately as UTF-8. Invalid encoding yields URI malformed; encoded `%23` remains a literal path character. Decoded path cannot begin `/` or contain NUL or `?`. Resolve relative to the origin directory (empty path means origin itself), discard empty/`.` segments, resolve `..` without crossing repository root. No query-string stripping, extension guessing, case normalization or path renaming is performed. - A missing fragment or empty fragment targets line 1–1 of the verified same-side text object. A nonempty fragment matches the first eligible ATX heading line whose normalized text equals that decoded fragment. Eligible headings begin at column one with one to six `#` followed by one ASCII space, outside the excluded/inline-code text above. Remove the leading hashes and one space, lowercase the remainder, remove every character except Unicode letters/numbers, ASCII spaces, underscore and hyphen, then replace EACH ASCII space with a hyphen. Do not trim/collapse spaces, add duplicate suffixes or normalize the requested fragment's case. Duplicate headings select the first matching line. Missing matches yield heading fragment unresolved, even when a platform's richer Markdown renderer would resolve another slug. Identity construction substitutes pending only in snapshotId members, as defined above. These vectors specify compatibility behavior; they do not claim richer Markdown/semantic analysis or an actual provider operation. ## Story table compatibility These additive tables share the existing SQLite connection and `reviews.id` membership. # Review-loop presentation

**Parent:** [Review-loop behavior](README.md)

## React and design principles

Implement the UI in React only. Do not add Svelte, Svelte components or a React/Svelte adapter. The user selected decompozr/design-system as a source of guidelines and design principles, not a component dependency. The reference package's component-installation instructions do not override that decision.

Apply the reference guidelines: restrained neutral hierarchy, meaningful limited color, related controls close together, readable Inter/monospace roles, visible keyboard focus, text alongside status colors, consistent spacing, clear loading/error/recovery states and at least 44px coarse-pointer targets. Own domain meaning and behavior in this product. Record the guideline source revision and check actual React output against it; do not claim package-component integration.

React components consume view data and collect user intent. Application/domain interfaces own submission, persisted state and validation. Selection/draft are local presentation state; cross-subsystem stream wiring remains centralized. Choose the appropriate React pattern by need without prescribing render props.

## Screen and states

Show a PR/base/head identity header, before-left and after-right source panes, a selected-span label, question composer and ordered discussion. Label removals/additions/modifications in text as well as red/green/yellow. Show question/reply author and source identity; state labels distinguish saved, delivery pending, notified, working, answered and delivery unknown. Attachment pending/revoked disables delivery with an actionable message while preserving saved content.

Keyboard users can select or specify an exact source span, reach the labeled composer, submit once and follow evidence links. Announce state updates politely without moving focus; errors associate with their fields. Submission preserves the draft until acceptance/readback or explicit rejection and avoids duplicate actions while in flight. No responsive layout can hide source attribution or uncertainty.

## Integration acceptance

Test the actual React controls in a real browser: labeled input, click and keyboard submission, disabled/busy behavior, props updates, repeated mount/unmount and listener cleanup. Inspect that only one application intent is emitted and no duplicate notification is caused by rendering. Review visual output against the guidelines and principles separately from automated behavior checks.

The product E2E starts the real app with task-local data, prepares pinned own-PR source, attaches the responsible session, asks through real controls, observes CLI notification/MCP reply and reads authoritative UI state. Independently test stale attachment, wrong anchors, duplicate commands, unknown notification and restart. Browser interaction, real CLI/MCP delivery and unfamiliar-reviewer comprehension are separate evidence.

## Implemented presentation decisions

The first view presents complete prepared documents in two independently scrolling panes. Pure source comparison assigns unchanged, removed, added and modified statuses; line markers and accessible labels accompany neutral/red/green/amber paint. The application view model carries these statuses into React. A line button selects one line; labeled side/start/end controls select an inclusive range. Source links retain immutable identity and update the selected span without moving an existing question.

Submission uses one application-owned command identity. An interrupted acknowledgement retains it for an unchanged retry; changing the unresolved submission is rejected until reconciled. The bridge reads at the accepted receipt's revision before clearing the draft. React Strict Mode remount and bridge route tests verify teardown/reconnect; rendering never schedules CLI work. Polling changes only view snapshots, while durable inbox delivery remains gateway-owned.

The controlled-host screenshot was inspected against design-system guideline revision `6cfe720df1a981e8ce8bb053927aea20d12f105d`: neutral hierarchy, readable source/discussion, explicit status/limits, text change markers, visible source attribution and focus treatment. Automated keyboard/source-link interaction passed. This is implementer visual review, not human comprehension or physical touch/screen-reader acceptance.

## Review read ownership

Explicit login and command receipt readback own their in-flight review request. A managed background poll must skip every in-flight read, including another poll, rather than aborting or replacing it. This preserves the login result used to initialize the semantic review scope when the owner opens an imported review. A later successful background review projection cannot substitute for that explicit authorization handoff.

Foreground operations retain latest-intent ownership: a newer explicit credential or snapshot choice may supersede an older request, and generation/publication fences still reject stale responses. The polling guard belongs only to the managed background route; it must not drop an authoritative login, selection or receipt readback. Disposal still aborts owned reads and tears down polling.

Disposal releases the canceled read's ownership slot immediately, even when its transport ignores or delays abort settlement. Reconnection or a new explicit login can own a fresh request without waiting for that obsolete transport. The disposed request's generation and controller identity remain fenced: a late success/failure cannot publish into the new lifetime or clear a newer request slot. Only actual disposal releases a canceled slot this way; background polling still cannot interrupt an active foreground read.

## Explicit bounded context controls

Before preparing declarations, the owner may leave the per-side context file cap blank to retain the default128, or enter an explicit integer1–128. Required before and after paths are independent exact repository-relative paths, one per line. Empty lines are omitted; spaces within nonempty paths, submitted order and duplicates are preserved in the command. There are no automatically chosen paths, implied allowlists or manufactured neighbors. The public command validates combined path counts, unique required counts versus the cap, and safe path/cap values before creating work.

Explain beside these controls that required paths are acquired first and remaining capacity follows the loader's stable ordering. The cap limits acquired sources per side, not the complete known inventory. A smaller cap can exclude known sources and makes incoming search scoped. It does not raise compiler budgets or establish repository-wide absence. Show each job's effective cap, and separate pending preparation and prior admitted corpus accounts with prepared/known/excluded/missing/unsupported/unvisited counts. Complete ledger and coverage remain accessible; do not label excluded source as scanned.

An unresolved command locks the form and exposes the unchanged-intent retry. The application captures submitted scope/cap/path arrays immutably, so edits or private navigation cannot alter its retained command identity. Historical facts, notes and exact-source inspection remain pinned while a new bounded preparation runs. Native input constraints provide immediate numeric feedback; authoritative validation and error recovery stay at the public application/gateway boundary.

A lowered cap may exclude changed paths from prepared analysis context as well as unchanged context paths. Only explicitly submitted required paths have required acquisition status. This never removes paths from the immutable original imported snapshot or its source browser.

A public query may supply a prepared corpus before any analysis is admitted. Label that current preparation account as pending preparation, not admitted facts. Other retained prepared context without an admitted analysis is a prepared corpus account. Reserve the admitted account label for the corpus accompanying the displayed admitted analysis.

An analysis object can also retain an unavailable result without an admitted graph. Require its positive analyzed status before using admitted account labels or suppressing the matching preparation account; truthiness is insufficient. A newer unavailable preparation does not erase a prior displayed analyzed result: show that result's admitted corpus and the distinct preparation corpus/status separately.

The same status distinction applies to declaration-list and previous-facts copy. An available prepared inventory is a prepared declaration list until it accompanies displayed analyzed facts. Do not promise that previous admitted facts remain when none exist.

Set `REVIEW_SOURCE_SPEC` to that file, `REVIEW_EXPECTED_SNAPSHOT_ID` to current read from the authoritative review, and `REVIEW_COMMAND_ID` to one stable unique command identity. Run `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/add-snapshot.ts` with the same `REVIEW_DATA_DIR`. The utility builds source outside ingress, sends AddSnapshot without an owner credential; it prints only the receipt. An unchanged retry uses the same command ID. A rejected receipt is durable; correcting rejected input needs a new command ID. Inspect a stale expected-current conflict rather than overwriting automatically.

The gateway independently reconstructs the manual manifest from local immutable Git objects before apply. Encoded JSON including metadata is limited to 8 MiB, distinct from per-read/source budgets. Unsupported schemes, forged IDs/content and unavailable required Git objects cannot admit new source. Exact already-retained snapshots and existing receipts remain idempotent when acquisition later becomes unavailable. This route has no provider discovery, import job UI or automatic source refresh.

The browser holds its selected snapshot while current advances. Explicit selection updates the URL’s snapshotId so reload reopens that source. A nonempty draft or unresolved submission blocks changing snapshots. Evidence links resolve their original snapshot; follow-up creates a separate anchored question with a parent link and both snapshot labels. Source addition never requests an agent turn. Restart verifies original preparation against retained history, then exports current. Back up/copy old SQLite before an owner-approved runtime migration, retaining credentials and unknown attempts. Never reset the pilot to pass migration.

## Controlled browser review captures

For an already running isolated candidate, `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/capture-review.ts` uses existing Chrome through the project Playwright dependency. Set private `REVIEW_DATA_DIR` and a unique external `REVIEW_CAPTURE_DIR`. The helper opens a fresh credential-free browser, captures the actual graph and its accessibility tree, and emits separate nonsecret candidate/target identity metadata. It does not reuse a personal browser session or imply native participant acceptance.

By default it captures only the graph before source drilldown. Optional `REVIEW_CAPTURE_PATH`, `REVIEW_CAPTURE_SIDE` and one-based `REVIEW_CAPTURE_START`/`REVIEW_CAPTURE_END` open a requested source through the actual UI and capture source identity and panes. `REVIEW_CAPTURE_FOCUS` selects a file in the complete index without opening source. `REVIEW_CAPTURE_CONTEXT`, `REVIEW_CAPTURE_SPANS` and `REVIEW_CAPTURE_UNRESOLVED` set to `1` expose those actual graph views. Root keeps separate diff/source captures and source-informed answer keys out of a fresh graph reviewer's first packet until its account is frozen. Artifact paths are operational evidence, never source-of-truth policy.

The current focused graph uses fixed card geometry and separate nonoverlapping span rows. The complete file index remains keyboard accessible and reports side availability even when no node can be rendered. Source opens are explicit; choosing a graph focus never silently moves a draft.

## Semantic core candidate

The slice04 core candidate adds authenticated analysis command/query/context-source routes and an owned fixed Node TypeScript6.0.3 worker. It preserves compiler7.0.2 for checks. The gateway starts import and semantic runners against one private SQLite effect lease; shutdown signals both before awaiting their actual owned work. Analysis and clarifications do not create agent notifications. This is candidate functionality, not a deployed pilot update or native/human acceptance.

Public commands/queries, immutable identities, limits and restart decisions are defined in [semantic meaning](semantic-graph.md) and [semantic persistence](semantic-storage.md). Manual snapshots need an explicit local worktree locator and declared sourceProject. Provider snapshots use their retained identity and matching import locator or an explicit replacement locator. A context analysis does not modify the snapshot or refresh provider heads.

An isolated UI/E2E owner may use the committed `tests/semantic-fixture.ts` helper to create a new private real-Git fixture and store, then `createGateway(store, controlledNotify).listen(0)` to choose an unused gateway port. The helper returns its private root, token in memory, pinned snapshot and exact RequestAnalysis value; do not print the token. Serve the candidate React app using the existing `scripts/ui.ts` with an independently selected unused REVIEW_UI_PORT and that gateway's loopback URL. Use reviewId=r. Close the gateway before the store, and remove only that fixture's owned root after preserving evidence. This synthetic fixture verifies integration/navigation; it is not the required actual ownPR understanding task. Existing pilot data, ports, credentials and routes remain separate.

The React candidate presents “Function neighborhoods” beside the existing review/source workspace. Expand “Acquire verified pinned context,” supply the explicit locator/manual source project when needed, prepare declarations and choose each side independently. Follow accessible caller/callee/evidence lists or the bounded focused canvas; the exact source inspector has an explicit return action and preserves the question draft. Inspect unknown dispatch, coverage and the complete source account. Clarifications are visibly attributed static-source explanations, not compiler fact edits or observed test runs. Existing retained analyses stay available while a new preparation waits; opening source pins that historical analysis until explicit navigation. This test-candidate journey still requires actual ownPR comprehension and independent full-slice acceptance.

The semantic MCP transport exposes analysis_get, analysis_source_get and graph_clarification_put through the existing stdio server after session_attach. A controlled SDK client must verify the actual tool catalog and deny source access before attachment, then read admitted facts, fetch exact immutable context and commit/retry an attributed clarification. Revocation must reject both reads and exact-receipt replay, and these operations must produce no wake/inbox item. Use a new private fixture and gateway/launch reference; this protocol evidence is separate from native host registration and the existing pilot attachment. Agents receive no context-acquisition or declaration-selection MCP tool.

### Imported review authorization handoff

Opening an imported review through the actual React action must initialize both its review and semantic query scope without a reload. Mounting the new review bridge and interval polling must preserve the explicit workspace-open request until its authoritative result is available. Verify the resulting semantic query carries the imported review and exact snapshot scope without an owner credential, then verify declaration preparation is enabled. This handoff check does not imply that acquisition, inventory or analysis will succeed within their independent limits.
