## Authority and provenance

All narration is authored content. The app validates identity, references, bounds and authorization; it does not prove that the prose accurately interprets its citations. The rail and step show who wrote the account, when, which immutable snapshot/version it concerns, and the basis of each claim. Keep these categories separate:

| Basis | Meaning and display |
|---|---|
| Source-linked observation | Author's statement linked to exact retained source. Valid coordinates/hash establish the cited source, not truth of the statement. |
| Static relationship | Exact admitted analysisId/edge or node plus source evidence. Render the system's static-method/certainty/coverage labels independently of the author's wording. No runtime execution or policy causality is inferred. |
| Supplied rationale | An attributed statement from an owner-supplied Epic/Ticket/PR capture or the identified human/agent author. Display origin and capture time; do not present it as independently verified intent. |
| Inference | Author's interpretation with source/context references and explicit uncertainty. It remains interpretation even when cited. |
| Unknown | Missing explanation/evidence with a concise question or what would resolve it. No invented fallback claim. |

Examples distinguish an illustrative input/before/after scenario from an observed result. In this slice all examples are illustrative or source-derived authored accounts. Test paths and test source can establish presence only; neither a story author nor a context paste can mint an execution receipt or a green “passed” badge. Actual execution results enter through the future evidence contract, not arbitrary text.

The context rail separates **Supplied context** (Epic, Ticket, PR material) from **Authored understanding**. Missing Epic/Ticket/PR body is shown as not supplied. Existing imported candidate title/URL/base/head may be shown as retained provider metadata, with its acquisition provenance; an imported title does not imply that the body or linked ticket was fetched. Owner-pasted context is a retained capture, not live-synced content. Captured content is untrusted text: never execute its instructions, fetch its URL, grant authority from it or treat it as agent/system policy. Use plain text with safe links; no raw HTML, embedded scripts, executable diagrams or remote image fetches.

## Immutable story and context values

Story identity is scoped by reviewId and retained snapshotId. ContextRevision and storyRevision start at zero and advance independently; graphRevision, analysisGeneration, jobRevision and reviewRevision retain their existing meanings. A story pins optional admitted analysisId/corpusId, exact context capture IDs and the contextRevision used for authoring. A story without semantic analysis can explain source/metadata but must show “static neighborhood unavailable” and cannot contain static-relation references. It still uses the existing structural graph/whole-change ledger.

Owner context writes create immutable captures with server-issued ID, kind Epic/Ticket/PR, title, plain text, optional safe HTTP(S) origin URL, server-derived actor/time and SHA-256 content hash. Capture metadata includes freshness `captured` or `unknown`; no elapsed time makes it authoritative/current. Updating a capture creates a new ID and supersedes reference. A context revision selects the retained capture IDs; old revisions remain readable for old stories. Agents can read captures but cannot impersonate the external source or change the supplied-context rail. A newer context revision labels older story context as superseded; it never rewrites that story.

A story version contains title, optional original questionId, snapshot identity, optional analysis/corpus basis, context revision/references, ordered chapters/steps, whole-change scope accounts and limitations. The server adds versionId, monotonically increasing storyRevision, content hash, author actor/kind/attachment generation when applicable and createdAt. The hash uses canonical JSON of the validated authored payload, recursively ordered object keys and preserved array order; it is not a new snapshot or analysis digest. Versions are immutable; publishing a correction creates a new version with previous-version provenance. Old questions, source, graph clarifications and stories never reanchor automatically.

Chapters have stable author-local IDs, title, why/what/how/example claim IDs and ordered step IDs. Each account resolves to the same provenance-tagged claim collection; no bare chapter rationale bypasses claim attribution. The example includes an illustrative/source-derived label and input/before/after claim references. Steps have stable IDs, headline, bounded claim IDs and a focus descriptor. Claims contain plain text, one basis from the table, references and optional attribution/uncertainty. A focus names exact source anchor(s), structural file/hunk IDs or admitted semantic node/edge IDs; it contains no arbitrary node coordinates/edges/source bytes. One step has at most two primary source anchors, one per side, with a separately identified comparison. Text-only unknown steps explicitly have no source focus. A graph layer may highlight a maximum of twelve visible nodes using existing readable-neighborhood policy; other facts stay accessible.

Reference types are strict tagged values: retained snapshot source (snapshot/side/path/contentHash and exact line span); semantic source (snapshot/corpus plus the complete semantic UTF-16/line anchor); static node/edge (analysisId plus existing fact ID); supplied capture (captureId/contentHash and optional exact text range); retained PR metadata field; or clarification ID plus its exact revision and analysisId. No mutable current pointer, local file path, prose URL or guessed identifier substitutes for evidence. Snapshot LF-based line spans and semantic parser coordinates remain distinct formats; use their owning validators, not arithmetic conversion that breaks CRLF/U2028/astral text. Validate every static and semantic reference through retained authorized04 read ports. Clarification text remains attributed interpretation when cited.

Primary comparison/file keys and structural hunk IDs use the [exact structural identity recipes and complete vectors](persistence-compatibility.md#structural-comparison-identity-compatibility), including manual fallback and copied comparisons. Each primary changed-file ledger key from `graphFiles(snapshot)` has exactly one scope account: a primary chapter with a short explanation, or an explicit unexplained reason. A file may be referenced by other steps without increasing coverage. Preserve copy/rename comparison keys and repeated identical provider source occurrences; never deduplicate the stored manifest or confuse a copied comparison with its modified original. Existing hunk/disposition coverage is rendered from source, not recreated or claimed narrated by story counts. Missing/binary/empty/unsupported files remain accessible scope rows; no fabricated line1. More than512 primary files is explicitly unsupported by this bounded story contract, never silently truncated into a whole-PR claim.

## Authoring and read protocol

These implemented operations use strict public domain schemas, the existing SQLite owner, authenticated gateway ingress and the existing attached participant's MCP transport. No app-hosted model, API key, real-time service, new conversation or session fork is introduced. Context/story publication is a bounded durable value write, not a repository process job and does not acquire the shared execution lease.

| Operation | Input and apply semantics |
|---|---|
| PutStoryContext | User only: commandId, reviewId, snapshotId, expectedContextRevision and bounded capture create/supersede/selection intent. Validate retained snapshot and origin/text limits; append captures and context revision atomically. Agents/bootstrap cannot write supplied context. |
| PublishStory | User or active attached agent: commandId, reviewId, snapshotId, expectedStoryRevision, contextRevision, bounded complete story payload and optional replacesVersionId. Pin only retained source and admitted analysis. CAS storyRevision and the authoring context revision; reject stale context with `story_context_conflict`, stale story with `story_conflict`. Do not use unrelated graph/review/job revisions as CAS. |
| Story query | Authorized reviewId/snapshotId, optional exact versionId, minimumStoryRevision and minimumContextRevision. Return selected published version summary, requested exact version, current snapshot/analysis markers and explicit newer-version/context indicators; unmet minima are `revision_unavailable`. Query never moves a selected source/history pointer. |
| Story context query | Authorized reviewId/snapshotId and optional exact contextRevision/capture ID. Return bounded retained captures with provenance. No external fetch or arbitrary path read. |

Command IDs and author-local chapter/step/claim IDs are nonempty strings of at most128 characters; revisions are nonnegative integers. PutStoryContext has exactly one action: `create` with one capture (kind/title/text/optional originUrl/optional supersedesCaptureId), or `select` with an ordered list of retained capture IDs. Create atomically selects the new capture, replacing only its named superseded capture when present and preserving other selections; more than16 selected captures rejects. Select may remove a capture from the current rail but never deletes retained data. Duplicate/foreign/supersedes IDs reject. PublishStory supplies the complete authored value, not an arbitrary patch; every chapter/step/claim/focus/scope reference must resolve in that value or retained evidence. Example scenarioKind is `illustrative` or `source_derived`; neither author-controlled value permits observed-execution badges.

Each command has a bounded ID, canonical actor/payload fingerprint and durable receipt. Recheck authorization before receipt replay. Exact authorized retry returns the original result; changed actor/payload conflicts. Receipts contain commandId/actorId/applied-or-rejected, reviewId/snapshotId, storyRevision/contextRevision, optional new version/capture IDs, result and typed error. They are not graph/job receipts with a renamed revision. Append body, pointers and receipt in one short transaction after bounded validation/encoding; recheck retained membership/authorization/CAS inside. No transaction waits for an agent, browser, source process or external context.

Attached agents may publish only for their authorized review and current attachment generation, as derived from credentials. They may create an initial story or revise the story series they authored; its initial author remains the series owner when a user appends a correction. A user may supersede any version with preserved provenance. A different attached author receives `story_author_conflict`; the user can publish an attributed account through owner ingress instead. Transfer of series ownership and collaborative authorship are deferred, not silently inferred from attachment replacement. Bootstrap is never an author. Do not allow caller-supplied actor/timestamp or `verified:true`. Replacing attachment does not alter story authorship, and revoked generation cannot read/write/replay through the former capability.

A new graph clarification or analysis request does not conflict with a story write. A story may cite a retained earlier admitted analysis explicitly; publication labels that basis historical if it is no longer selected. Source history advancing likewise does not invalidate a historical story. Publication updates the snapshot's available current story pointer but never auto-selects it in an already-reading client. The client announces a newer story/context and offers an explicit open action. If an older reference is unavailable/corrupt, reject new publication; existing readback reports broken evidence rather than substituting current source or invented text.

Reuse the existing AskQuestion → durable addressed inbox/CLI delivery → same-session MCP read/reply flow. “Ask for an explanation” collects the user's question and an actual selectable snapshot source anchor, then submits one normal AskQuestion intent through the review bridge with the new bounded recovery contract below. The reviewed028 bridge stores pending identity only in memory; recoverable reload is required05 work, not an existing04 capability. It does not create a new correction inbox, notification type or background authoring job. Publication may link the exact questionId from the same review/snapshot, but does not mark it answered or establish that the answer is useful. A generic SDK reply that merely acknowledges transport cannot pass the explanation task. The author must address the user's trigger/why, before/after, consequence and limits with relevant evidence; independent review judges that quality. Expose new MCP `story_get`, `story_context_get` and `story_publish` through the already attached capability, deriving review ownership as in current tools. Only the explicit user question uses the existing addressed-request delivery route; unknown delivery retains its existing non-replay policy.

## Resource bounds and persistence

Bound text and structures before expensive reference resolution: at most16 current captures,8 KiB text per capture,128 KiB encoded context command; eight chapters,32 total steps,128 total claims, eight references per claim/step and256 unique evidence references per story; title/headline120 characters, claim1200, scope explanation400, total encoded story command256 KiB. All IDs/references are finite strict values; malformed arrays/duplicate local IDs/dangling steps/chapter or scope refs reject. Context/story inputs cannot raise server limits. The existing8 MiB gateway envelope is not permission to accept unbounded authored output.

Retain at most8 MiB canonical encoded context capture/revision and story-version bodies per review, counting each immutable body once, including text/escaping/provenance/scope/facts references. Exact boundary passes; the next new write rejects atomically with `story_storage_limit`, retaining prior history. Owner test limits may only lower. No silent eviction, pruning of cited evidence or automatic compaction of a story into different content. Receipts, private browser state and the rest of SQLite are separate from this body quota; this is not an all-database resource guarantee.

Use new owner-held story/context tables and receipts through `createStore`; other subsystems never open SQLite or read storage internals. Source/semantic evidence validation uses bounded public ports and indexed lookups once per unique reference. Retained reference facts are immutable and may be checked outside the transaction; authority/CAS/body equality recheck inside. Domain owns content policy and transitions, application owns view/player state, UI renders. Existing import/analysis process leases, schemas and resource limits stay unchanged. Restart reads authoritative versions/receipts without rerunning acquisition, analysis or agent turns.

## Player, reading and exploration

The slim bottom-center player has one row: drag handle, previous, replay/pause, next, step number and chapter selector. Icons have accessible names/tooltips; text carries story information. Keep44px coarse-pointer targets even when visual chrome is slim. Controls remain operable at narrow width; chapter labels may shorten with full accessible names, never hide step/navigation. A keyboard move/reset alternative makes dragging optional. Position is private, clamped inside the visible viewport/safe-area, restored on resize and resettable; dragging never navigates or alters shared state.

Player state is application-owned: exact review/snapshot/storyVersion, chapterId/stepId/index, mode (`paused`, `playing`, `exploring`, `ended`), elapsed step time, highlight/displayed evidence, selected comparison/source and an optional exploration return frame. Initial load is paused. Explicit Replay replays the current step's highlight from time zero and continues in story order across chapter boundaries; while playing the same control is Pause. Previous/next moves one step in global story order, chapter choice selects that chapter's first step, and either pauses for reading. Step number shows the global position/total with the current chapter label. Default playback advances after eight seconds of visible active time per step; the final step ends paused/ended, with no loop. No duration controls, audio or authored executable timing language are added.

Reading actions pause: focusing/selecting narration (not focus inside the playback controls), user scrolling the source/context rail, activating evidence, dragging the player, switching Flow/Diff, hiding the page or losing the active review connection. Preserve elapsed time; no hidden-tab catch-up. Reduced-motion uses immediate highlights and starts paused, and never removes information. Replay is an explicit time-zero action; “Resume story” after exploration restores its saved cursor/elapsed value in paused mode, so it cannot advance before the reviewer is ready.

Entering exploration first freezes one return frame containing the exact story version/chapter/step/elapsed cursor, graph focus/expanded IDs/viewport, displayed source/comparison/selection and original draft identity/anchor/text. Exploring other nodes, source, chapters through ordinary source navigation or supporting files does not overwrite that frame; explicit story navigation exits exploration after restoring/confirming pending draft rules. Resume restores the frame, not the latest current graph or newest story. Exploration can have its own private selection/draft; never replace a dirty or uncertain submitted draft with the saved one. Preserve both scoped drafts and require explicit choice/reconciliation when switching which composer is active. The pending-submission recovery contract below requires exact unchanged retry/readback before retargeting, including after reload.

Story focus and question draft anchor are distinct. Playback may change displayed evidence through an explicit user play/step action, but cannot silently retarget an existing question/draft. “Ask about this step” is a separate intent and respects pending/dirty composer state. Import completion, analysis admission, context/story publication and polling never move the story cursor, active source snapshot, private selection or draft. Explicit user history/version change pauses and stores the old private frame; opening a newer story starts paused rather than borrowing old chapter IDs.

Basic mobile Flow (graph/story) and Diff (source) presentations share the same application state. Switching is reading/exploration, not a second story instance; preserve cursor, pause, return frame and draft. Before/after identities stay available on narrow screens without a toggle that changes source identity. Full mobile tuning, semantic zoom, sophisticated motion and4K polish remain later scope.

Retain a bounded tab-session view checkpoint (sessionStorage, at most64 KiB encoded UTF-8) of private IDs/cursor/position/return-frame and unsent draft text (at most8 KiB per active/return draft), never bearer credentials, full source, story/capture bodies or process data. This is tab-local recovery, not account sync or shared canonical state. On reload validate against authorized retained records and pause before showing; unavailable/stale selection gets explicit recovery without guessing an anchor. Oversize unsent drafts remain complete in memory, are omitted from this view checkpoint and visibly marked unavailable after reload; never truncate a draft. If storage is unavailable/full, unsent view state can remain in memory with an explicit recovery-unavailable message. This best-effort rule does not permit sending an uncheckpointed question.

### Pending question recovery across reload

The review application owns the public recovery seam, separate from story publication and the import bridge. The minimum contract is `getQuestionRecovery()` (safe state/identity), `recoverPendingQuestion()` (explicit action under the current authenticated credential) and the existing `ask` operation extended with write-ahead persistence. These are current application public exports; the earlier028 memory-only submission implementation did not provide them. UI passes intent through them; it never reads/writes pending storage directly or reconstructs an AskQuestion command from a restored draft. No new server job, inbox category, credential service or receipt endpoint is required: retry uses the existing `/api/commands` receipt path; readback uses the authorized retained-review query.

At most one unresolved question command is retained per tab. Before any first network send, the bridge validates the immutable anchor and text using the existing AskQuestion policy (trimmed nonempty text at most16 KiB UTF-8), constructs the complete command once, and persists its exact serialized request and SHA-256 fingerprint. The request includes type, commandId, reviewId, original snapshot/anchor, exact text and optional parentQuestionId. Preserve original bytes on every retry; the server retains its own canonical normalized receipt fingerprint. These are distinct hashes, not interchangeable proof of acceptance. The checkpoint also contains schema version, private originalDraftId, credential scope, phase, and any accepted receipt. The public ask intent carries this stable private draft identity separately from its server command; it is not an added AskQuestion wire field. It contains no bearer, full source or copied story. Cap the request at128 KiB and the entire encoded pending record at256 KiB, independently of the64 KiB view checkpoint. Bounds include JSON escaping; oversized metadata or raw whitespace rejects before send rather than truncating or weakening existing server validation.

Persist one complete record with atomic sessionStorage replacement, then read it back and verify equality before dispatch. Unavailable storage, quota failure or failed equality means **unsent**: retain the draft and show recovery storage unavailable; no network mutation occurs. Unknown-schema/corrupt pending records are quarantined visibly and cannot be converted into an ordinary resubmittable draft. A hash detects accidental mismatch, not malicious storage tampering; the server remains authoritative for all commands and authorization. Browser data deletion, tab closure and independent duplicate tabs are outside this tab-reload recovery guarantee; do not claim global duplicate-intent detection.

Credential scope is the SHA-256 of a domain-separated, length-delimited tuple containing the browser-facing location.origin and the exact trimmed bearer used for authentication, computed in memory. Persist only this hash. It is a local matching guard, never an authentication credential or an authority assertion; actorId alone is insufficient because multiple credentials may name the same actor. The authenticated public review read must succeed before recoverable draft details are hydrated or a recovery action is enabled. The token always remains memory-only. A new login increments the live bridge generation and invalidates old promises; matching the stable scope allows explicit recovery across that generation change, never automatic adoption/send. Capture the in-memory credential and live generation for each effect; recheck generation and pending fingerprint after checkpoint work and immediately before dispatch. Never read a later mutable token to send an earlier intent. Response/checkpoint writes likewise require the captured generation and exact pending identity. A different credential, origin, unauthorized review or failed authentication leaves the pending command locked and sends nothing, even if the actor name matches. Offer re-entry of the original credential; never migrate/rekey or mint a new command on the user's behalf.

| Pending phase | Required behavior and transition |
|---|---|
| `awaiting_ack` | Persisted before first send, so crash-before-send and lost acknowledgement are conservatively indistinguishable. Reload shows unresolved submission, with no auto-resend. After explicit authorized same-scope recovery, send the exact stored bytes and commandId through normal ingress. The same server receipt is returned if already committed. Editing a composer cannot change this record or create a replacement command. |
| `accepted_awaiting_readback` | On an applied receipt, retain the exact receipt including commandId/actorId/revision/cursor/questionId/eventId and original payload, and checkpoint this phase before reporting completion. Recover by reading the original retained snapshot with minimumReviewRevision equal to receipt.revision. Match questionId, actor, normalized text, full anchor and optional parentQuestionId; revision alone is insufficient. If a persisted receipt cannot be validated, retain unresolved state rather than fabricate completion. |
| Confirmed applied | Only matching authorized readback completes the submission and removes the pending record. Mark the original draft as submitted; it cannot reappear as an ordinary unsent draft from an older view checkpoint. Update/invalidate that draft checkpoint before removing the pending record; if either storage update fails, retain the pending record so another explicit recovery is harmless. Do not erase an unrelated exploration draft. |
| Confirmed rejected | A matching authoritative rejected receipt for this exact command can release the pending guard and retain the draft for an explicit corrected new intent. A `command_conflict`, identity mismatch, malformed reply or transport/authentication error does not prove the original unknown command was rejected; keep it unresolved. |

If persisting the applied-receipt phase fails, keep the already durable `awaiting_ack` record and the receipt in memory. Explicit retry after reload still uses the same command; it cannot append a second question/event. Never clear a previously uncertain command merely because a later attempt returns HTTP400/401/403. If accepted readback fails or is stale, preserve the accepted revision/receipt and retry reads without resending; no new ID. No caller may turn an unresolved pending record into a fresh submission by changing text, source, story, login or component lifetime.

Recovery reads are keyed to the original command's review/snapshot and captured credential generation. They reconcile status independently of the currently displayed historical source; they do not retarget the composer, move the story cursor or replace the selected snapshot. Preserve the existing pending guard against new question submission/source retargeting. Reloading into another history URL may display that history read-only while the pending command remains visibly recoverable for its original source. A late response from an old login/disposed bridge cannot update the view, clear a newer record or attach an old receipt to another command. Reading the original source for reconciliation is not implicit navigation to it.

Explicit logout clears the bearer, invalidates the generation and removes the ordinary view checkpoint. Retain the noncredential pending record in a locked state until explicit same-scope recovery; a “logged out” view reveals no saved draft body. This narrow exception prevents logout/login from making an uncertain question look unsent. Existing import explicit-login intent-clearing remains unchanged: it does not own or clear this review-question recovery record. Closing/clearing tab data can discard local recovery, so the app must never label that discard as a server-side cancellation or permission to resend a previously unknown intent. No automatic resend occurs on reload, reconnect, mount or story playback.

## Managed routes and acceptance meaning

Register story/context-committed → authorized story view and story-focus intent → coordinated graph/source view through the integration registry. Coalesce polling views only, not accepted commands. Route scope includes review, snapshot, credential generation and connection lifetime; old responses cannot publish after logout/dispose/history/version change or clear a newer pending intent. One owned playback clock exists only while playing; teardown cancels it, aborts reads and removes listeners/routes. Mount/remount never publishes a story, launches work or sends another question. App shutdown retains normal durable records and existing process-owner behavior; the story layer owns no child process.

Acceptance asks whether a fresh reviewer can give a correct bounded before/after account, trace a real consequence, distinguish rationale/inference/unknown/execution and account for the rest of the PR, then investigate and resume without manual reconstruction or lost work. Controls, source coverage and citations alone cannot pass. Freeze the initial actual story/graph-first account before source inspection, compare/correct it afterward and retain misconceptions/effort. Native automatic delivery, meaningful attached-agent answer and unfamiliar-human observation remain separately assessed. Before accepting slice05/720p, reflect on actual code/structure, promote learned knowledge and close a fresh whole-current-product docs-only rebuild audit excluding plans/chat/code.


## Exact authoring core value contract

Status: accepted derivation for 05A; implementation and independent review evidence live in the slice checkpoint. This section defines DTO meaning, not executed acceptance. All objects are strict (unknown keys reject), IDs are nonempty strings of at most128 characters, hashes are lowercase SHA-256, repository paths are bounded relative paths, and revisions are safe nonnegative integers. Text preserves its exact validated bytes; object-key ordering alone is normalized. No author/timestamp/execution fields are accepted in authored inputs.

`StoryContent` contains `title`, optional `questionId`, optional paired `analysisId`/`corpusId`, ordered `captureIds`, `chapters`, `steps`, `claims`, `scope`, and `limitations`. `PublishStory` carries that value under `story`, plus command/review/snapshot IDs, `expectedStoryRevision`, `contextRevision`, and optional `replacesVersionId`. The replaces pointer, when supplied, must equal the current version; the server always records the actual previous version. Analysis/corpus must identify the same admitted result, including historical results. A question must belong to the same snapshot.

A chapter has `id`, `title`, `why`, `what`, `how` (each a claim ID), `example` (`scenarioKind`, `input`, `before`, `after`, with the last three claim IDs), and ordered nonempty `stepIds`. Every step occurs in exactly one chapter and has `id`, `headline`, nonempty `claimIds`, and `focus`. Every claim has `id`, `text`, `basis`, bounded `references`, optional `attribution` and `uncertainty`. Basis tags are `source_observation`, `static_relationship`, `supplied_rationale`, `inference`, `unknown`. Source observations require snapshot/semantic source references; static claims require a static node/edge reference plus source evidence matching each cited fact; rationale requires a supplied capture or attribution `author` (the server author) with no invented identity; inference requires evidence and uncertainty; unknown requires uncertainty and cannot claim source verification. Supplied rationale with captures remains attributed to their retained origin. Chapter/scope/step IDs resolve exactly; unattached claims reject.

Reference tags and fields are: `snapshot_source` (`anchor` in existing LF snapshot coordinates, `contentHash`); `semantic_source` (`corpusId`, complete `anchor` in owning UTF-16 coordinates); `static_node`/`static_edge` (`analysisId`, `factId`); `capture` (`captureId`, `contentHash`, optional paired UTF-16 `start`/`end`); `metadata` (`field` from title/prUrl/repository/prNumber/baseSha/headSha); `clarification` (`analysisId`, `clarificationId`, exact `revision`). No metadata body field exists. Hashes, nonempty ranges and retained membership are checked. A capture must be selected in the story's exact context revision and listed in its captureIds. Semantic/static/clarification references require the story's exact analysis basis; semantic corpus must match it.

Focus tags are `none`; `sources` with one/two snapshot-or-semantic source references (one per side) and exact primary `fileKey`; `structural` with primary `fileKey` and optional exact `hunkId`; `semantic` with one static reference and one/two exact source references. Source comparisons must match the primary changed-file paths for their sides; semantic focus must cite the selected node body/declaration or edge target/site, rather than an unrelated source. `none` is permitted only for a step whose claims are unknown. Scope tags are `explained` (`fileKey`, `chapterId`, `explanation`, nonempty evidence references) or `unexplained` (`fileKey`, `reason`). Exactly one row covers every graphFiles key, including copied comparisons and unsupported/empty files. Explained rows require source/static/capture/metadata support; the app validates identity, not prose truth. Limits are120 characters for titles/headlines,1200 for claim text/uncertainty,400 for scope explanation/reason,128 claims,32 steps,8 chapters,8 references per claim/scope/step and256 unique references overall. IDs, arrays and text are bounded before reference reads.

`PutStoryContext` carries command/review/snapshot IDs, `expectedContextRevision`, and `action`: strict `create` with `capture` (kind `Epic`/`Ticket`/`PR`, title, plain text, optional credential-free HTTP(S) originUrl, optional supersedesCaptureId), or `select` with ordered unique captureIds. Capture text is at most8KiB UTF-8; at most16 captures are selected. Supersession must name a currently selected capture. Content hash is SHA-256 of the exact capture text. The server creates captureId/createdAt/actorId; freshness is `captured` for a supplied URL and `unknown` otherwise. Create/select always advances context revision, including an unchanged explicit selection; no implicit no-op or deletion is inferred.

`storyQuerySchema`: reviewId/snapshotId, optional versionId/minimumStoryRevision/minimumContextRevision. `StoryView` returns those IDs, currentSnapshotId, currentAnalysisId, storyRevision/contextRevision, `currentVersion` summary, `version` (exact requested or latest, or null at revision zero), ordered version summaries, `newerVersion`, `newerContext`, `historicalAnalysis`, `staticNeighborhoodAvailable`, `basisUnavailable`, and `brokenEvidence` (bounded references/reasons). A missing requested version yields `story_version_unavailable`; unmet minima yield `revision_unavailable`. `storyContextQuerySchema`: reviewId/snapshotId, optional contextRevision/captureId. `StoryContextView` returns currentContextRevision, selectedRevision, selectedCaptureIds, captures and missingKinds. `StoryReceipt` contains commandId/actorId/state/reviewId/snapshotId/storyRevision/contextRevision, bounded result (new versionId/captureId when applicable), and optional typed error. ### Browser scope compatibility vector

Schema1 scope uses the browser UI/proxy-facing `location.origin`, not the separate internal gateway listener URL. An injected test origin is used literally. Apply ECMAScript String.trim to the bearer and no Unicode normalization. Encode `pr-reviewer-credential-scope-v1`, one NUL byte, decimal UTF-8 origin byte count, a colon, the exact origin, decimal UTF-8 trimmed-bearer byte count, a colon, then the exact trimmed bearer. There is no extra separator between the origin and the following length. Hash all resulting UTF-8 bytes with SHA-256 to lowercase hex. Only that digest is persisted; it is not authentication. Origin/credential mismatch locks existing records without automatic rekeying.

| Nonsecret conformance input | Exact value |
|---|---|
| Origin | `https://review.example:7443` (27 UTF-8 bytes) |
| Input bearer, JSON escaping | `"\u00a0 café-🔑 \t"` |
| Trimmed bearer | `café-🔑` (10 UTF-8 bytes) |
| Preimage, escaped NUL | `pr-reviewer-credential-scope-v1\u000027:https://review.example:744310:café-🔑` |
| SHA-256 scope | `c32dba39d6d0a60deccbfaa1cbd6bf5842dee07b20f6cdafed24b3e499ccf08f` |

Trimming the shown surrounding whitespace preserves this digest. A different port/origin, different bearer, or decomposed accent changes it. The pending request fingerprint separately hashes its exact stored request bytes; it is neither this scope digest nor the server's normalized receipt fingerprint.

### Source inspection, issue triage and evidence

Semantic inspection initially shows the exact selected UTF-16 span with retained identity. Full-file expansion and return preserve that selection and do not mint a snapshot question Anchor. Selected issues default to actual path/declaration/anchor membership from public admitted facts and existing diagnostic/reason codes. Keep complete global/unassigned warnings and full counts discoverable; no new inferred edges, severities or resolution claims. Snapshot source uses LF lines, semantic source uses its owning offsets, and provider/controlled fixture/execution provenance stays distinct.

05C engineering requires actual Chrome server commit→deliberately dropped acknowledgement→reload→same-credential explicit recovery with one actual question/event and one controlled notification, plus accepted-receipt/lost-readback recovery with zero resend. A generic thrown request or database restart is insufficient. Controlled notification proves only that exercised gateway route, never native-host causality. Independent review, final actual PR24 story/graph A→source B, meaningful attached answer, code-informed720p reflection and fresh whole-product docs-only audit remain root-coordinated gates.


### Composition owner fence learned from core review

The workspace composition has its own credential/navigation/lifetime generation in addition to each child bridge's generation. Every login, logout, disposal and superseding explicit navigation invalidates old workspace continuations. Capture exact credential/generation before awaiting the public review login/read; recheck before accessing its resulting view and before starting either child login. Selecting/opening/resuming sources likewise rechecks the composition owner after each await and before child effects or returning a navigation success. A correctly fenced child response does not by itself authorize an older composition continuation to read a newer child's current view and reinstall the old credential. No extra fetch, credential persistence or authentication service is introduced.


Resume is transactional at the application view boundary: keep the first return frame and exploration draft active while exact snapshot/story/cursor/semantic source/evidence restoration is being validated. Publish the consumed frame/original active draft/paused restored view only after every required read succeeds under the same composition/controller intent generation. A rejection, unavailable retained record or superseding user/login/disposal intent retains the frame and both drafts for explicit retry. Partial reads never establish a completed return, and no newer selection repairs a missing retained source.

Public async draft selection also captures the credential, controller generation and selection intent before reading another snapshot. Recheck before each following effect and before publishing retained draft bodies. A newer login/logout/navigation/disposal must never expose an older credential's private drafts, even when an aborted transport resolves. A return-frame read uses the same intent fence through every readiness phase.

Pending removal compares the complete immutable identity: exact stored request bytes (therefore its command identity), origin, review, scope, draft and fingerprint, with compatible receipt phase. A record whose body no longer equals the verified submitted record remains quarantined in place; a matching fingerprint field alone cannot authorize deletion. Removal and ordinary draft invalidation remain conservative after any mismatch. No distributed-tab coordination is implied.

`semanticIssueProjection(view, focus, sourceAnchor?)` derives the selected issue view in the application layer. An explicitly inspected source anchor takes precedence; otherwise the focused admitted declaration supplies its exact body anchor. Unresolved sites match the exact caller identity or overlapping same-side/path/hash UTF-16 span. Diagnostics match same-side/path and their supplied start offset within that span. Context issues match the selected side/path; context issues without a path or side remain visibly global/unassigned. Complete unresolved, diagnostic and context collections and their counts remain accessible separately, including warnings assigned to other files. This filtering changes presentation only and never changes retained facts, reason codes, severity or completeness claims. Public workspace `openPath(path)` owns default selectable source choice; React submits a path rather than choosing a side or manufacturing its first-line Anchor.

Story semantic-source hydration and staged evidence restoration use the existing authorized read port, POST `/api/analysis/source`, with the exact strict review/snapshot/corpus/side/path/hash query body. This POST is a retained-source read, not an analysis command, acquisition or worker wake. The gateway does not provide a GET alias; tests and actual semantic-story journeys must exercise this wire contract rather than accepting an invented query URL. A failed read leaves the return frame retryable.

Explicit snapshot navigation during exploration preserves the first frame and original draft. It reanchors only an empty active exploration draft to the new snapshot's actual selectable default source; a nonempty active draft blocks source replacement. Explicit retained-draft choice preserves both bodies while selecting its own snapshot under the async owner fence. No unchanged old-snapshot Anchor may silently become a composer selection against the new source.

`AnalysisBridge.openSource(anchor, {intent?: "inspect" | "restore"})` preserves the existing exact authorized read. Its public `sourceNavigation` projection distinguishes normal explicit inspection from application-owned restoration. React performs its established inspector heading focus/scroll only for `inspect`; `restore` lets the single story owner restore its saved page position after readiness, without minting source authority or suppressing genuine reading focus. Both modes retain source-read credential/generation/selection fences. The semantic map frame also records `fullSource` as a presentation choice alongside the exact selected anchor; restoration preserves that expansion while the source selection itself stays exact. A normal newly inspected anchor defaults to its selected span.

The workspace registry also owns `structural-map-view-to-private-frame` and `semantic-map-view-to-private-frame` routes. Public `captureMap(kind, snapshotId, frame)` accepts UI-local map presentation input only for the currently authorized, matching review/story snapshot. Semantic capture supplies the actual public analysis-view snapshot, so an old analysis render cannot checkpoint itself against another source. Routes collect view state without commanding focus, source reads or workers, expose bounded diagnostics and dispose with the workspace. Story restoration remains the one owner of restore identity and does not subscribe directly to map internals.

An omitted oversized draft remains explicitly unavailable after reload through subsequent ordinary checkpoints. An empty recovered text field does not silently erase its omission marker; replacement text, exact submitted-draft invalidation or explicit ordinary-view reset releases that marker. Private view schema validation also requires unique draft IDs, an existing active draft with the displayed snapshot Anchor, matching cursor/version identities and a valid separate original/exploration frame reference. Structurally valid but inconsistent private identities remain quarantined before hydration.

Connecting the workspace presentation must preserve an already-owned explicit pre-mount login. Disconnect/logout/superseding navigation invalidate continuations; first mount alone is not a new credential or navigation intent. React mirrors the actual authorized displayed review/snapshot into the browser URL when that read model changes, rather than waiting for slower optional child views. Reload at a visibly selected historical source must reopen that source, including during semantic/story reads; a background pinned refresh cannot select a different URL source. Controlled rejected-command fixtures supply the full public receipt identity/actor/revision/cursor/result shape, so receipt parsing never treats a legacy incomplete stub as authoritative rejection.

All added checkpoint-validation and staged-return reads are owned effects, not just generation-fenced continuations. Story owns one staged resume slot, rejects duplicate Resume before another read, and cancels that slot on a superseding private intent or lifetime interruption while retaining its frame. Its request controllers are tracked and aborted on interrupt. Public `ReviewBridge.readSnapshot(snapshotId, signal?)` accepts an optional caller lifetime signal; the workspace forwards it unchanged, and the review owner also tracks/aborts auxiliary authorized reads on logout/login/disposal/source replacement. The optional signal does not authorize another source or change read membership. Exact pending commands remain immutable and retained through cancellation; cancelling a read is not proof that an earlier command failed. Shared AnalysisBridge readiness remains owned by that subsystem; a disposed story stops awaiting/applying it without starting a duplicate fetch or cancelling another owner's shared selection.

A restored semantic inspector starts an operation-specific authorized source read: `AnalysisBridge.openSource(anchor, {intent?, signal?})`. The caller signal cancels that exact source operation and releases its loading slot, even when transport ignores abort; source publication checks the operation controller and current source owner again. A superseding source read is owned separately and cannot be cancelled or cleared by the older caller. Story passes its validation/resume signal through this port. Cancelling only the story's await is insufficient: an orphaned delegated source response could otherwise restore the old inspector after a new exploration intent. Shared analysis selection readiness remains independent and is never cancelled merely to force a new focus.

### Startup hydration selection ownership

Workspace login authorizes the exact review first, completes the initial AnalysisBridge credential/snapshot login read, and only then starts StoryBridge login and private-view hydration. Recheck the captured workspace credential/generation/lifetime between these public-port awaits. Story restoration may legitimately select an exact retained analysis instead of the initial unpinned current-analysis view; those selection owners must not overlap as parallel child logins. This sequencing prevents an expected selection handoff from surfacing as a failed workspace login. It adds no request, fallback-current source, worker effect or second state owner.

Current-owner authentication/query/transport failures remain observable through their existing public error/rejection paths, including a transport AbortError that has not been superseded. Do not filter by error name or message. A login continuation or rejection from a superseded workspace credential/lifetime cannot publish an interaction error for the replacement login or start later child effects. Child publication/abort/shared-readiness fences remain independently required. Missing retained private source/analysis still exposes the recovery limitation and preserves its checkpoint; it is not repaired with current source or a swallowed error.

A hydrated return frame is published only after its exact retained semantic selection/source readiness and the other private-view validations succeed. The first enabled Resume uses that ready frame and the existing staged restore ownership; startup cannot expose a partly hydrated frame as ready. During startup, a frame that has not completed validation supplies no enabled Resume action. A successful normal hydrate/resume must not leave a false startup abort alert. This behavior does not assert that a previously reported first Resume failed: the independently established defect is the earlier parallel-login hydration rejection, before Resume was invoked.

# Guided explanations and exploration

**Contract revision:** `review-story-v1`, planning amendment 4 (measured reading hierarchy and explicit question intent; existing semantic ports preserved)

**Date:** 2026-10-24

**Direction:** Implemented bounded authored story/context, React player, exploration/resume and private question recovery. This maintained contract describes the current owner and formats; bounded engineering is independently reviewed. Actual combined own-PR comprehension/meaningful answer, whole-product knowledge audit and full05/720p acceptance remain separately gated.

**Parents:** [Vision](../vision.md), [experience constraints](../architecture.md), [source presentation](presentation.md), [semantic facts](semantic-graph.md), [retained semantic state](semantic-storage.md), [participant ownership](../participant-adapters.md)

## The smallest useful story

A reviewer should be able to explain the actual change, its purpose or the limits of known purpose, one concrete before/after example, and an important consequence without assembling the narrative from scattered source. A short authored story leads with graph/source highlights and explains those highlights in plain English. It accounts for supporting files and exposes unknowns. It is not a generated call graph with decorative prose, a correctness verdict or an execution report.

The first implementation supports one selected story version per retained review snapshot, at most eight chapters and thirty-two steps. A useful initial story usually has three chapters: the reviewer-visible change, the important mechanism/consequence, and supporting changes/evidence/remaining questions. That is an authoring guideline, not a hard-coded generic story that fits every PR. Every chapter includes a brief why, what/how and concrete example. An unsupported why is explicitly unknown or attributed to its author; it is never inferred as fact from a function name or citation. A whole-PR account may admit that some files remain unexplained.

A step presents its matching plain-language account beside a compact graph/source focus, with both visible in one coherent application state. The reading order gives meaning before expanded source bodies; graph-led means that the account points to real highlighted evidence, not that code must precede its explanation. It may focus a verified static relation, a source/file/hunk comparison or a context-backed explanation. Authored rationale never becomes a compiler edge. Preserve before-left/after-right, red removal, green addition and yellow modification with non-color labels. An absent side stays absent; no before/after mode toggle or API/Helpers orientation selector is added. Repeated import-header excerpts are poor explanations: select actual relevant source/body spans and explain the decision they support.

## Explanation and investigation requirements learned from use

A useful static neighborhood can accurately show a new constructor dependency and unchanged neighbors while leaving the actual user consequence, request policy and lifecycle unexplained. Preserve that factual success and its limits. The story must supply an inspectable source-backed account of the decision and a concrete before/after user example, separating authored explanation from verified static bindings. An edge does not prove request authorization, teardown, business purpose or observed execution; missing support stays unknown. A source-corrected account is not evidence that the initial graph-first presentation already conveyed it.

Complete file inventory is necessary but cannot be the whole-change explanation. Use existing chapter membership and primary scope accounts to group the change by responsibility, with a concise source-backed reason for each group and visible unexplained material. Supporting docs/config/tests remain part of that account. No separate grouping taxonomy, inferred ownership engine or per-file semantic edge is needed. Acceptance requires a fresh reviewer to summarize central/supporting responsibilities and one real consequence without assembling a narrative from filenames and long function bodies.

Exploration initially shows issues associated with the exact selected declaration or source path; retain clear all-issues access and counts. Group only existing diagnostic codes/causes and distinguish incomplete-context findings from other reported issues without inventing severity or suppressing them. Entries with no reliable selected-source association remain explicitly unassigned/global, never falsely unrelated or resolved. This is a bounded projection over admitted facts and their existing coverage, not new analysis or a complete unresolved ledger claim beyond the returned data.

The source inspector foregrounds the exact selected span with side/path/commit/corpus/hash and applicable coordinate format, then offers full-file expansion. Preserve context needed to interpret the span and an explicit return to the original focus/scroll/selection. Highlighted-span selection and source availability are separate from question anchor permission; unchanged semantic-only context does not become a fabricated legacy snapshot anchor. The goal is less filtering and source scanning while keeping every available fact, warning and source route inspectable.

## Reading hierarchy and explicit investigation intent

**Design amendment:** 05D, derived from an actual graph-first review of candidate `67b24f3`. The central conceptual account was correct, but a fresh agent rated overall cognitive effort burdensome. Large excerpts appeared before their explanation; chapter details repeated current claims; whole-change scope exposed machine tuple keys; graph placement required checking the relationship list; inspected source and the independent question anchor were easy to confuse. This is qualitative single-agent evidence, not a human study, a false-edge finding or a measured time saving. The following is the corrective interaction contract; delivery remains gated separately.

The primary job is to understand a change and its consequence before deciding what to investigate. Preserve the incumbent React surfaces, colors, typography, evidence and subsystem owners. Reduce competing presentation, rather than adding another summary layer, generated rationale or a new information model.

- A selected step starts with its chapter/step identity, the current plain-language account and its consequence or example when authored. Show the claim's source-observation/static/inference/unknown attribution and material uncertainty beside that account. Do not fabricate a consequence when absent. Compact focus labels and an evidence disclosure follow the explanation; an unopened long source body must not push the entire explanation below the story panel's first viewport on desktop or narrow layouts. The reviewer may scroll the page to the story panel; this is not a promise that every global control fits above it.
- Render each exact claim ID once within the current account and expanded chapter-detail area. Chapter details add why/what/how/example material not already displayed, with clear labels; if already displayed, refer to its existing location or omit the duplicate rather than repeat it. Distinct claims with similar wording remain distinct authored claims; presentation must not rewrite their meaning or treat textual similarity as identity. Missing rationale and uncertainty stay visible. Compact claim provenance remains available without opening the full source body.
- Before/after evidence is available through a clearly labeled, initially collapsed disclosure showing side, path and selected range. Opening it presents the exact selected span, then an explicit full-source route, retaining existing provenance, LF versus UTF-16 coordinate labels and missing-side explanations. Evidence disclosure, source reading and chapter detail reading pause playback. An explicitly opened source remains readable until the reviewer changes focus or closes it; playback does not auto-expand a wall of code. No retained source, reference or scope entry is discarded to make the page shorter.
- The whole-change account starts with existing chapter responsibility groups and counts, their authored meaning, and an explicit unexplained group. Each expandable group lists every primary file exactly once with its human-readable repository path, change status where retained, and authored explanation. Distinguish renamed before/after paths when available. Resolve labels through the exact retained file identity; expose the original machine key in technical details, never use tuple serialization as the main file label. Unknown identity remains visibly unavailable rather than guessed. Group membership is the existing authored chapter assignment, not a new dependency/ownership classifier. Counts reconcile to the complete immutable scope. A generic responsibility is not proof of understanding that file's actual change; authoring must supply a specific source-backed role or declare the gap unexplained. The app does not invent those explanations.
- A static graph uses compact function identities, side/change/context labels and legible directed caller-to-callee relationships as its default. Function bodies are available on explicit inspection rather than occupying every node. The selected function, its direct incoming/outgoing relations and unknowns must be recognizable without deciphering source boxes or consulting another list to discover direction. Preserve before-left/after-right and all admitted relationship IDs, call-site evidence and limits. Placement is a layout, not execution order, lifecycle order, causality or a fabricated edge. Cycles/unknown calls remain truthful; this bounded refinement does not add a new graph algorithm or increase analysis coverage. The accessible relationship list remains a peer navigation route, not the only explanation of canvas direction.
- Evidence inspection and question composition have independent, persistently visible source labels: snapshot, side, path and range. If they differ, say so next to the investigation/composer handoff. An explicit **Use this range for question** intent is available only for an exact question-eligible retained snapshot anchor. It previews old and proposed anchor, preserves text and parent question, and delegates through the existing workspace/draft owner. For a nonempty unsent draft, require explicit confirmation of that anchor replacement; cancel leaves everything unchanged. This applies to the active exploration draft and never overwrites the captured original return-frame draft. An in-flight or unresolved pending command remains immutable and blocks retargeting, with an explanation. Confirmed submitted text does not become an unsent replacement draft. A semantic-only/unchanged source without an owner-validated snapshot mapping cannot be used as an invented question anchor; explain the unavailable action. Opening a reference, focusing a graph node, publication, background refresh or reading source never implicitly applies this intent.

The one-row draggable player, step number, keyboard/focus behavior, reading pause, mobile synchronized Flow/Diff, red removal/green addition/yellow modification with non-color labels, exact story/source/draft return frame, private recovery and authority contracts remain binding. New disclosure or anchor-confirmation controls need accessible names, keyboard operation and visible focus. In narrow layouts a long story title may wrap, while the adjacent Flow/Diff labels remain on one line and retain their controls. Keep independent UI critique separate from tests and screenshot geometry. A successful correction requires a fresh graph/story-first account frozen before source/key, source comparison, an explicit cognitive-burden verdict and the meaningful question/reply/return journey; a shorter screenshot or passing DOM assertion alone does not establish understanding.

### Derived reading and question-intent ports

The React surface consumes the application-owned `storyPresentation` alongside the existing story projection. Chapter detail entries are ordered why, what, how, example input/before/after and deduplicated by exact claim identity against the selected step and earlier detail entries. Scope labels resolve `graphFiles` by the exact retained file key, including rename before/after paths and retained status; they never parse an arbitrary tuple as trusted identity. Groups use existing chapter membership and the authored what-claim, plus a separate unexplained group. Every original scope account and reference remains available; a missing mapping receives an explicit unavailable label and retains its technical key.

`questionEvidenceProjection` reports ready, blocked or unavailable. Ready requires an authenticated active unsent draft, exact snapshot-source reference, matching retained source hash and valid snapshot LF anchor. The proposed anchor snapshot must equal both the active/displayed story snapshot ID and the loaded snapshot object ID. Historical evidence from snapshot S while T is active is unavailable, even if its path and body hash match. Adoption never navigates across snapshots or leaves a private draft anchored to another snapshot; the unavailable reason points to explicit snapshot navigation instead. Pending or submitted drafts are blocked. Non-source and semantic-only references are unavailable for this bounded port; no UTF-16-to-LF conversion or fabricated snapshot mapping is added. The read model carries the exact evidence, active draft, proposed anchor, mismatch indication and whether nonempty text needs confirmation. React displays the proposal and collects confirmation; it does not decide eligibility. The explicit `adoptEvidence` application operation rechecks the current proposal against the supplied one, including text, parent, draft identity, source reference and anchor. A changed proposal is superseded and must be inspected/confirmed again. Pending state is checked before adoption. Confirmed adoption preserves draft text/parent/identity and original return frame, replaces only the active draft anchor, removes the old comparison key and pauses. It creates no command or receipt and does not change persisted private-session formats. No ordinary navigation path gains this exception to the nonempty-draft source guard.

The semantic application exposes `semanticRelationshipProjection` over the existing bounded semantic projection. It retains each admitted node/edge identity, labels caller-to-callee direction from those facts, and supplies incoming/outgoing names only for displayed edges. With no explicit valid focus it marks the existing first neighborhood seed selected. Empty lists say no resolved relationship in this projection, not no caller/callee in the repository. React chooses compact geometry and inspection controls; the selected marker shares the function heading, and both called-by and calls direction lines keep their own visible row. Long names may truncate within a line with their full label retained for inspection; selection styling must not collapse or hide either direction. Business and fact-selection policy stays in the application. Source inspection, complete evidence lists, unknowns, corpus bounds and the graph's twelve-node presentation cap are unchanged.

## Inherited semantic and read interfaces

The implemented semantic application public surface includes `createAnalysisBridge`, `AnalysisBridge`, `SemanticView`, `semanticProjection`, `semanticExcerpt` and `semanticSourceKey`. Its explicit snapshot/optional analysis selection, focus, exact-source open/close, context request/declaration choice, cancellation, clarification, unchanged retry and managed connect/diagnostics are distinct operations. Opening source pins its admitted analysis; background admission does not replace that inspection. The visible neighborhood cap12 limits presentation, not accessible fact coverage. The current StoryBridge owns player, draft and return-frame coordination; AnalysisBridge remains the semantic selection/source owner consumed through public ports.

Context preparation accepts an explicit per-side cap1–128 with default128 and exact required-priority arrays, bounded at64 combined submitted entries. Preserve submitted order/duplicates in command identity even though loader requiredness deduplicates/sorts. A lower cap is neither an allowlist nor repository-wide coverage; remaining slots follow deterministic acquisition order and exclusions stay in the complete known account. Prepared context/inventory, positive analyzed/admitted facts, unavailable results, full changed-source inventory and currently visible nodes are separate states. Story playback neither changes a cap nor launches preparation to manufacture coverage.

Review background polling skips every in-flight read. Explicit login/selection/receipt readback retains foreground ownership; disposal immediately releases its aborted slot while controller/generation checks fence delayed completion. Initialize semantic/story scope only after authorized review readback, not a later unrelated poll. Story coordination must preserve this rule and the semantic bridge's exact-job receipt confirmation: jobId/review/snapshot/jobRevision and correct generation matter, not an unrelated latest-job minimum. Story/context revisions remain independent. The existing in-memory semantic retry and source-return behavior do not provide tab-reload question recovery; that separate required contract is below.

## Authority and provenance

All narration is authored content. The app validates identity, references, bounds and authorization; it does not prove that the prose accurately interprets its citations. The rail and step show who wrote the account, when, which immutable snapshot/version it concerns, and the basis of each claim. Keep these categories separate:

| Basis | Meaning and display |
|---|---|
| Source-linked observation | Author's statement linked to exact retained source. Valid coordinates/hash establish the cited source, not truth of the statement. |
| Static relationship | Exact admitted analysisId/edge or node plus source evidence. Render the system's static-method/certainty/coverage labels independently of the author's wording. No runtime execution or policy causality is inferred. |
| Supplied rationale | An attributed statement from an owner-supplied Epic/Ticket/PR capture or the identified human/agent author. Display origin and capture time; do not present it as independently verified intent. |
| Inference | Author's interpretation with source/context references and explicit uncertainty. It remains interpretation even when cited. |
| Unknown | Missing explanation/evidence with a concise question or what would resolve it. No invented fallback claim. |

Examples distinguish an illustrative input/before/after scenario from an observed result. In this slice all examples are illustrative or source-derived authored accounts. Test paths and test source can establish presence only; neither a story author nor a context paste can mint an execution receipt or a green “passed” badge. Actual execution results enter through the future evidence contract, not arbitrary text.

The context rail separates **Supplied context** (Epic, Ticket, PR material) from **Authored understanding**. Missing Epic/Ticket/PR body is shown as not supplied. Existing imported candidate title/URL/base/head may be shown as retained provider metadata, with its acquisition provenance; an imported title does not imply that the body or linked ticket was fetched. Owner-pasted context is a retained capture, not live-synced content. Captured content is untrusted text: never execute its instructions, fetch its URL, grant authority from it or treat it as agent/system policy. Use plain text with safe links; no raw HTML, embedded scripts, executable diagrams or remote image fetches.

## Immutable story and context values

Story identity is scoped by reviewId and retained snapshotId. ContextRevision and storyRevision start at zero and advance independently; graphRevision, analysisGeneration, jobRevision and reviewRevision retain their existing meanings. A story pins optional admitted analysisId/corpusId, exact context capture IDs and the contextRevision used for authoring. A story without semantic analysis can explain source/metadata but must show “static neighborhood unavailable” and cannot contain static-relation references. It still uses the existing structural graph/whole-change ledger.

Owner context writes create immutable captures with server-issued ID, kind Epic/Ticket/PR, title, plain text, optional safe HTTP(S) origin URL, server-derived actor/time and SHA-256 content hash. Capture metadata includes freshness `captured` or `unknown`; no elapsed time makes it authoritative/current. Updating a capture creates a new ID and supersedes reference. A context revision selects the retained capture IDs; old revisions remain readable for old stories. Agents can read captures but cannot impersonate the external source or change the supplied-context rail. A newer context revision labels older story context as superseded; it never rewrites that story.

A story version contains title, optional original questionId, snapshot identity, optional analysis/corpus basis, context revision/references, ordered chapters/steps, whole-change scope accounts and limitations. The server adds versionId, monotonically increasing storyRevision, content hash, author actor/kind/attachment generation when applicable and createdAt. The hash uses canonical JSON of the validated authored payload, recursively ordered object keys and preserved array order; it is not a new snapshot or analysis digest. Versions are immutable; publishing a correction creates a new version with previous-version provenance. Old questions, source, graph clarifications and stories never reanchor automatically.

Chapters have stable author-local IDs, title, why/what/how/example claim IDs and ordered step IDs. Each account resolves to the same provenance-tagged claim collection; no bare chapter rationale bypasses claim attribution. The example includes an illustrative/source-derived label and input/before/after claim references. Steps have stable IDs, headline, bounded claim IDs and a focus descriptor. Claims contain plain text, one basis from the table, references and optional attribution/uncertainty. A focus names exact source anchor(s), structural file/hunk IDs or admitted semantic node/edge IDs; it contains no arbitrary node coordinates/edges/source bytes. One step has at most two primary source anchors, one per side, with a separately identified comparison. Text-only unknown steps explicitly have no source focus. A graph layer may highlight a maximum of twelve visible nodes using existing readable-neighborhood policy; other facts stay accessible.

Reference types are strict tagged values: retained snapshot source (snapshot/side/path/contentHash and exact line span); semantic source (snapshot/corpus plus the complete semantic UTF-16/line anchor); static node/edge (analysisId plus existing fact ID); supplied capture (captureId/contentHash and optional exact text range); retained PR metadata field; or clarification ID plus its exact revision and analysisId. No mutable current pointer, local file path, prose URL or guessed identifier substitutes for evidence. Snapshot LF-based line spans and semantic parser coordinates remain distinct formats; use their owning validators, not arithmetic conversion that breaks CRLF/U2028/astral text. Validate every static and semantic reference through retained authorized04 read ports. Clarification text remains attributed interpretation when cited.

Primary comparison/file keys and structural hunk IDs use the [exact structural identity recipes and complete vectors](persistence-compatibility.md#structural-comparison-identity-compatibility), including manual fallback and copied comparisons. Each primary changed-file ledger key from `graphFiles(snapshot)` has exactly one scope account: a primary chapter with a short explanation, or an explicit unexplained reason. A file may be referenced by other steps without increasing coverage. Preserve copy/rename comparison keys and repeated identical provider source occurrences; never deduplicate the stored manifest or confuse a copied comparison with its modified original. Existing hunk/disposition coverage is rendered from source, not recreated or claimed narrated by story counts. Missing/binary/empty/unsupported files remain accessible scope rows; no fabricated line1. More than512 primary files is explicitly unsupported by this bounded story contract, never silently truncated into a whole-PR claim.

## Authoring and read protocol

These implemented operations use strict public domain schemas, the existing SQLite owner, authenticated gateway ingress and the existing attached participant's MCP transport. No app-hosted model, API key, real-time service, new conversation or session fork is introduced. Context/story publication is a bounded durable value write, not a repository process job and does not acquire the shared execution lease.

| Operation | Input and apply semantics |
|---|---|
| PutStoryContext | User only: commandId, reviewId, snapshotId, expectedContextRevision and bounded capture create/supersede/selection intent. Validate retained snapshot and origin/text limits; append captures and context revision atomically. Agents/bootstrap cannot write supplied context. |
| PublishStory | User or active attached agent: commandId, reviewId, snapshotId, expectedStoryRevision, contextRevision, bounded complete story payload and optional replacesVersionId. Pin only retained source and admitted analysis. CAS storyRevision and the authoring context revision; reject stale context with `story_context_conflict`, stale story with `story_conflict`. Do not use unrelated graph/review/job revisions as CAS. |
| Story query | Authorized reviewId/snapshotId, optional exact versionId, minimumStoryRevision and minimumContextRevision. Return selected published version summary, requested exact version, current snapshot/analysis markers and explicit newer-version/context indicators; unmet minima are `revision_unavailable`. Query never moves a selected source/history pointer. |
| Story context query | Authorized reviewId/snapshotId and optional exact contextRevision/capture ID. Return bounded retained captures with provenance. No external fetch or arbitrary path read. |

Command IDs and author-local chapter/step/claim IDs are nonempty strings of at most128 characters; revisions are nonnegative integers. PutStoryContext has exactly one action: `create` with one capture (kind/title/text/optional originUrl/optional supersedesCaptureId), or `select` with an ordered list of retained capture IDs. Create atomically selects the new capture, replacing only its named superseded capture when present and preserving other selections; more than16 selected captures rejects. Select may remove a capture from the current rail but never deletes retained data. Duplicate/foreign/supersedes IDs reject. PublishStory supplies the complete authored value, not an arbitrary patch; every chapter/step/claim/focus/scope reference must resolve in that value or retained evidence. Example scenarioKind is `illustrative` or `source_derived`; neither author-controlled value permits observed-execution badges.

Each command has a bounded ID, canonical actor/payload fingerprint and durable receipt. Recheck authorization before receipt replay. Exact authorized retry returns the original result; changed actor/payload conflicts. Receipts contain commandId/actorId/applied-or-rejected, reviewId/snapshotId, storyRevision/contextRevision, optional new version/capture IDs, result and typed error. They are not graph/job receipts with a renamed revision. Append body, pointers and receipt in one short transaction after bounded validation/encoding; recheck retained membership/authorization/CAS inside. No transaction waits for an agent, browser, source process or external context.

### Browser scope compatibility vector

Schema1 scope uses the browser UI/proxy-facing `location.origin`, not the separate internal gateway listener URL. An injected test origin is used literally. Apply ECMAScript String.trim to the bearer and no Unicode normalization. Encode `pr-reviewer-credential-scope-v1`, one NUL byte, decimal UTF-8 origin byte count, a colon, the exact origin, decimal UTF-8 trimmed-bearer byte count, a colon, then the exact trimmed bearer. There is no extra separator between the origin and the following length. Hash all resulting UTF-8 bytes with SHA-256 to lowercase hex. Only that digest is persisted; it is not authentication. Origin/credential mismatch locks existing records without automatic rekeying.

| Nonsecret conformance input | Exact value |
|---|---|
| Origin | `https://review.example:7443` (27 UTF-8 bytes) |
| Input bearer, JSON escaping | `"\u00a0 café-🔑 \t"` |
| Trimmed bearer | `café-🔑` (10 UTF-8 bytes) |
| Preimage, escaped NUL | `pr-reviewer-credential-scope-v1\u000027:https://review.example:744310:café-🔑` |
| SHA-256 scope | `c32dba39d6d0a60deccbfaa1cbd6bf5842dee07b20f6cdafed24b3e499ccf08f` |

Trimming the shown surrounding whitespace preserves this digest. A different port/origin, different bearer, or decomposed accent changes it. The pending request fingerprint separately hashes its exact stored request bytes; it is neither this scope digest nor the server's normalized receipt fingerprint.

## Single-owner workspace and recovery correction

The 2026-10-24 access correction supersedes product login/logout and credential re-entry language above. `createReviewWorkspace(...).open()` and the imports bridge's `open()` start credential-free owner lifetimes. The browser has no token/login/logout controls and emits no owner Authorization header. Existing low-level login(token)/logout functions remain programmatic compatibility/lifecycle seams only; no runtime owner credential is created or read.

Current private scope is SHA256 of UTF-8 domain `pr-reviewer-local-owner-scope-v1`, NUL, decimal UTF-8 origin byte length, colon and exact browser-facing origin. A nonsecret in-memory local-owner marker selects that scope and is explicitly omitted from request headers. Generation/controller/fingerprint fences, write-ahead storage and explicit exact-command recovery remain unchanged. A new open invalidates older effects independently of the stable owner scope. Older credential-scoped pending or private-view records remain preserved and locked when incompatible; explain legacy reconciliation without requesting the original token or silently replaying. Authoritative retained history still loads.

Story evidence and story store public calls accept either trusted in-process local-owner access or retained participant/user credentials. Gateway owner calls use the object, never a manufactured browser token; explicit agent credentials retain attachment and generation checks.
